title: Lead Data Scientist
description:
Job Reference: 718998The Curtin Institute for Computation (CIC) Computation now fundamentally underpins the majority of internationally competitive research across all fields and disciplines. As the demand for computational skills has grown, so too has the need for a dedicated institute that can support the research community. The Curtin Institute for Computation (CIC) was established to meet this increasing demand for computational modelling, data analytics, and visualisation. It initiates and fosters collaborative, interdisciplinary research and education programs with researchers. Our computational specialists assist in applying computational methods across the sciences, engineering, social sciences, health science, business, and the humanities to provide innovative solutions to complex problems.
Curtin Open Knowledge Initiative (COKI) The Curtin Open Knowledge Initiative is developing a broad program of work on the theme of ‘open knowledge institutions’. The goal of our project is to develop tools and data that will allow universities to understand how effectively they are operating as open knowledge institutions; and to support strategic change in higher education and research. Combining data science and a critical perspective we are addressing questions of how to collect and manage data at a large scale, as well as how sharing this data and analysis will effect the ecosystem.
Your new role We are seeking a detail orientated Data Scientist to join the Curtin Open Knowledge Initiative (COKI) team which sits inside the Curtin Institute for Computation. This role will support the COKI project deliver unique insights into bibliometric analysis, across Curtin and, increasingly, to external industry stakeholders. This position provides people and technical leadership to a team of data specialists who utilise a range of skills across mathematical, computer science and statistical disciplines in the provision of data analytics solutions for research and/or business areas of the University. Reporting to the CIC Director, the role will be to lead the COKI Team inside the CIC, as well as potentially other leadership responsibilities across the wider CIC team. Responsibilities will include:Applying data science methodologies to specific projects associated with the analysis of bibliometric data. In conjunction with the COKI team and CIC specialists, liaise with project partners and stakeholders to develop project scope, identify deliverables, timelines and risks, and to develop work plans. Using appropriate project management software initiation, planning and coordination of activities for assigned projects. Maintain communication with project partners and stakeholders throughout the duration of assigned projects, to ensure regular exchange of project related information and to initiate appropriate action for issues if they arise. Organise and facilitate project progress meetings within the COKI and CIC teams and with internal and external stakeholders. Leadership responsibilitiesLead the effective and efficient delivery of data analytics services which support and enhance research outcomes of COKI and the CIC. Provide leadership and mentoring to the team and fostering a work environment of high achievement, continuous improvement, and job satisfaction. Engage and influence key stakeholders on where data analytics can add value and identify opportunities for innovation in data exploration practices. Data Science responsibilitiesWork with the COKI and CIC research groups to understand where data analytics can add value. Prepare required data sets for sophisticated statistical analysis, model generation and derivation of actionable insights. Provide technical leadership and identify and use suitable technologies, tools and algorithms to be applied to the research problems under consideration. Build credible statistical models from the data and use best coding practices to generate reproducible work. Explore and visualise the data to present the ‘story’ of the data in a meaningful way, and to a range of technical and non-technical audiences. Assist researchers or business areas to employ data management best practice. You will bring to the roleA postgraduate tertiary qualification in statistics, mathematics, computer science or related discipline with considerable relevant experience or an equivalent combination of relevant experience and/or education/training. Demonstrated technical and people leadership skills to effectively manage a team of highly skilled and high performing data scientists. Demonstrated experience in a senior data science role and knowledge of the data analytics requirements of different research / business disciplines. Demonstrated High-level problem solving and analytical skills. Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to negotiate and consult with a diverse range of stakeholders. Strong experience in using languages, such as C and/or C++, Python, Perl, R, or shell scripts. Understanding of data science, computational methodologies and data management. In particular knowledge of SQL would be an advantage. Outstanding interpersonal and verbal communication skills with the ability to articulate technical concepts to non-technical clients. Well-developed written communication skills with the ability to construct clear and concise reports and correspondence. Strong organisational skills with the ability to operate autonomously as well as an effective team member. Demonstrated experience in data modelling and visualisation. Experience working with Agile development methodologies. Experience with Atlassian Jira would be an advantage. What we offer you Work on real world challenges across a variety of projects associated with research and academia Agile and flexible working environment with great work life balance The opportunity to grow, develop and diversify your own skill set Competitive remuneration package with 17% Superannuation For further information on Curtin’s employee benefits visit https://about.curtin.edu.au/jobs/Next steps Curtin University requires you to provide a cover letter and resume to include sufficient information and examples to allow us to assess your suitability for the role. Actively participate and assist in programs and projects to uplift ASIC analytics capability.
Contribute to setting the team's strategy and direction.

description:
School of Languages and Cultures
The School of Languages and Cultures has grown rapidly in recent years and now has over 1000 equivalent full-time students (over 8,000 course enrolments). It is one of the largest schools of language instruction in Australia with 46 fixed-term and continuing academic staff.
The School of Languages and Cultures teaches Chinese, French, German, Indonesian, Japanese, Korean, Russian and Spanish, as well as Linguistics and Applied Linguistics, to students in the Bachelor of Arts, Bachelor of International Studies, and the University-wide concurrent Diploma in Languages, the Diploma of Arts, and dual degree programs.

Staff research and supervise PhD students in these fields and also in Australian Aboriginal languages.
About This Opportunity
We currently have an excellent opportunity for a Language Data Scientist to join the School of Languages and Cultures. The Language Technology and Data Analysis Lab (LADAL) in the School of Languages and Cultures is driving the development of a series of national eResearch infrastructure projects, including the Australian Text Analytics Platform (ATAP) and the Language Data Commons of Australia (LDaCA), in collaboration with the NCRIS-funded Australian Research Data Commons (ARDC) and other key national partner institutions.
The primary purpose of this position is to provide support for building and utilising the digital research platforms and tools developed through these projects, including supporting the training of researchers in the use of these platforms and tools, and to engage in research on the development and use of language technologies.
This position is located at our picturesque St Lucia campus, renowned as one of Australia’s most attractive university campuses, and located just 7km from Brisbane’s city centre. Demonstrated evidence of a developing record of publication in high-quality outlets in the field.
Demonstrated skills in common programming languages, including Python and R.

Demonstrated evidence of an established record of publication in high-quality outlets in the field.
Evidence of ongoing research projects, including plans for external funding applications.

title: Data Scientist Proteomics
description: Children’s Medical Research Institute (CMRI) was Australia’s first dedicated paediatric research facility and is now one of the world’s most highly regarded independent medical research centres. Our research focuses on the areas of embryonic development and birth defects, cancer, neuroscience and gene therapy and we have a strong international reputation based on our research outcomes. It is also home to the world-first proteomics project, ProCan, which is changing the way cancer is diagnosed and treated. CMRI’s research programs are supported by state of the art facilities and committed research and support staff. Our achievements are made possible by a loyal network of community supporters, highly engaged donors and the very successful Jeans for Genes® fundraising campaign. A data scientist position is available in the ProCan Cancer Data Science Group, led by Dr. Qing Zhong. ProCan (the ACRF International Centre for the Proteome of Human Cancer) is a world-first initiative developed and launched in September 2016 by Professors Phil Robinson and Roger Reddel, and established with a $10 million grant from the Australian Cancer Research Foundation (ACRF). Equipped with six SCIEX mass spectrometers and a super computer (800TB / 480 cores), ProCan processes tumour samples through a proteomic method, SWATH-MS, which allows fast mass spectrometric conversion of small amounts of tissue (biopsy level) into a single, permanent digital file representing the quantitative proteome of the sample. One of the goals of ProCan is to measure thousands of proteins in about 70,000 cancers of all types with known treatment outcome and correlate tumour proteotypes with clinical phenotypes. The Cancer Data Science Group aims to develop novel computational tools and sophisticated machine learning algorithms to achieve this goal. Other major focuses of the group are 1) big proteogenomic data mining and management, 2) the genome-proteome association analysis and multi-omic data integration for studying cancer, 3) development of advanced statistical tools to account for batch effects caused by large-scale, high throughput proteomics, and 4) implementation of big data-driven, evidence-based computational tools to achieve predictive, preventive, personalized medicine. We invite applications from PhD scientists to join our group. Applicants should be experienced data scientists with a high degree of motivation in academic research, an excellent record of scientific accomplishments with publications in peer-reviewed journals, and the ability to work independently with outstanding communication and writing skills. Candidates should have a strong clinical/biological understanding and a background in bioinformatics, biostatistics or machine learning. Strong programming skills in R and Python are required. Previous experience in proteomics is essential. You will be responsible for conducting biostatistical analysis, performing scientific data visualization, developing solutions to proteomics research and cancer biomarker discovery. You will be provided with a competitive remuneration package in accordance with qualifications and experience. Additional benefits include the provision of a Public Benevolent Institution salary packaging scheme and participation in an employer-contributed superannuation fund. Publications in high impact journals can be expected. This is a full-time position for two years with the possibility of extension. Applications should include: A cover letter (citing PV2122) with statement of motivation and a detailed description of the qualifications described above,A curriculum vitae including a chronological list of publications Contact details (phone/email) of three professional referees and be forwarded to recruitment@cmri.org.au Applications will remain open until filled; however we encourage you to submit your application by Friday 21st May as we will interview suitable candidates from that date onwards - We reserve the right to withdraw this ad prior to the closing date.

Developing a variety of advanced quantitative methods related to the function, striving for continuous improvement. title: Data Scientist/ Research Scientist
description:
Besides MetService being New Zealand's National Meteorological Service, it's a successful global weather company. MetService is a technology-based organisation employing about 300 staff and headquartered in Wellington, New Zealand.
New Zealand's meteorological challenges are unique. Our lovely island country is narrow and mountainous, situated approximately half-way between the Equator and the South Pole. A lot of the time, New Zealand's weather results from the passage of mid-latitude weather systems. The rugged terrain influences the atmospheric flow; there can be large west-east differences in rainfall, temperature, etc., over short distances; likewise, the hills hugely influence the winds. In the summer months, cyclones from the South Pacific tropics can pass close by. And in the winter, we occasionally experience polar outbreaks. As far as the weather is concerned, there is never a dull moment.
We have a great opportunity in our Forecasting Research and Development (FR&D) team for someone enthusiastic about machine/deep learning (ML/DL) and statistical analysis.
If you are excited about participating in the meteorological application of statistical and machine/deep learning methods, and the development of operational systems, then this might be you.
We are seeking a Research Scientist having:An honours degree or above in mathematics or physics (postgraduate qualifications preferred)Knowledge of probabilistic statistical forecasting techniques and/or ML/DLFamiliarity with Linux, Amazon Web Services, high-performance computing; or, other experience with running operational forecasting systemsSolid software development skills (e.g. in Python, Julia) and experience in ML/DL libraries (e.g., Scikit-Learn, Flux.jl, TensorFlow)The ability to communicate technical ideas to non-scientific audiencesAlso, having experience with dynamical atmospheric modelling (e.g., WRF), meteorological observation, and climatological data sets would be an advantage.
Why join us? Aside from arguably the best views in Wellington from the top of the Botanic Garden, we enjoy achieving, we appreciate creativity and we recognise everyone's unique skills and qualities. If you are not in Wellington, there is the option to work from home. The Forecast Research and Development team is a diverse group of scientists. We all multi-task, supporting a range of activities from implementation of an idea in prototypes, to high-quality software development of operational applications, to agile support of customer requests and support of operations. We look forward to hearing from you!If this role sounds like you, please click "Apply Now" to submit your application including CV and cover letter.

title: Data Scientist
description:
Data Scientist (214586) OUR COMPANY At Boehringer Ingelheim we develop breakthrough therapies and innovative healthcare solutions in areas of unmet medical need for both humans and animals. As a family owned company, we focus on long-term performance. We believe that, if we have talented and ambitious people who are passionate about innovation, there is no limit to what we can achieve; after all, we started with just 28 people. Now, we are powered by 50,000 employees globally who nurture a diverse, collaborative and inclusive culture. THE POSITION The role of the Data Scientist is to work within the Customer Engagement & Insights Business Unit (CEIBU) and across the Prescription Medicine business to extract, integrate, and analyse data to generate insights to understand and engage with our customer's and optimise the customer experience. The Data Scientist works closely with other members of the Customer Engagement & Insights BU and brand teams to present data insights in both the form of regular reporting metrics and customer insights to inform the creation and optimisation of customer journeys and to identify behaviours within customer segments as part of the Integrated Customer Plan. The Data Scientist is responsible for bringing key stakeholders together to think about key questions that can be answered by bringing data to life to generate actionable insights that drive business strategy. Ultimately, the Data Scientist will create change and an insights driven culture to ensure business decisions are made based on sound information. Tasks & responsibilities Data Management This involves the identification, extraction, cleansing, formatting, and integrating of disparate data sources and analytics and transform available information streams from BI’s Go-To-Market platforms. Collaborate with the Customer Engagement & Insights BU, BI’s global team, 3rd party data providers including agencies, and brand teams to identify the relevant data needed to create business insights. Ensuring the usage of data sources falls within the compliance obligations across BI and our customers. Insight Generation Bring stakeholders together regularly using the Data Science Life Cycle methodology to think about key questions that can be answered through data interrogation. Create an insights culture and drive the change by facilitating conversations that help to generate insights and regularly present insights based on proactive analysis of business scenarios. Regularly monitor and analyse campaigns to understand the performance of various channels being used and the extent of content engagement including gaining an understanding of why content has performed in a certain way (e.g. local content vs. global content). Assess customer behavior along the course of a campaign to identify the customer’s segment, preferences of channel and content, attitude towards a particular therapy and products, and additional insights to help create a 360 customer view and to help develop suggestions for next steps of interaction with the customer. Undertake data analytics, using understanding of commercial drivers and experience in business optimization, to provide expert advice whilst considering the current business landscape and challenges. Working closely with CEIBU and respective brand teams to optimize digital content through tagging, SEO, SEM, search words and to offer cross-content recommendations. Run the BI Data Science Life Cycle methodology, collaborating across brand teams and BI’s business to communicate insights and to optimize customer journeys and to create regular forums on how campaigns are performing and how customers are behaving so as a business we’re in a constant state of learning and taking action to improve customer engagement and business outcomes. Measurement and Reporting Identifying, developing, and setting the appropriate KPI’ in agreement with the business to measure ourselves against in customer campaigns and customer engagement and regularly communicating this through easy to interpret reports. Using various tools and data workbenches to run analyses and extract data to perform a 360 customer view to aid segmentation and customer journeys. Accountable for reporting campaigns outcomes against objectives, with rationale for variations and recommendations for optimization. Establish internal digital benchmarking and comparisons against industry performance, with accompanying rationale for any variations. Ownership of digital reporting schedule to ensure on-time delivery of inputs and outputs (locally and globally) and report design for the relevant internal audience. Sharing and communicating of results at relevant internal forums to ensure best practice learning amongst the Brand Teams. Produce data visualisations and intuitive graphics to present complex analytics. Requirements Experienced data scientist and general marketing analytics expert with experience in extracting and formatting data from digital platforms. Familiar with pharma analytics as well as the nature and design of insightful test and learn scenarios. Proven ability to create insights by manipulating and integrating different data sources. Independent thinker and subject matter expert. Excellent communication skills and the ability to facilitate discussions with senior management to drive change and communicate insights in business language to a broad range of stakeholders. Passion for data and the ability to generate excitement about what the data is saying. Advance Excel skills such as data summarisation with Pivot Table, dynamic Data Visualization, data Query/Connection, and Power Query Editor. Experience with using Data Science programs, such as R, Python and SQL for data preparation and transformation (ETL), run statistical tests and experiments, Machine Learning models for prediction and segmentation. Experience in managing multi-person tasks, achieving quality and timeliness Bachelor’s Degree in Pharmaceutics or relevant fields/studies Pharmaceutical industry experience is key, although Banking, Finance, FMCG and Digital Agency industry experience will be considered. title: Senior Data Scientist
description:
About us    Over the next 40 years, Sydney’s population is projected to swell to over 12 million residents and regional NSW will accommodate an extra 700,000 people. Transport for NSW is delivering an unprecedented $72.2b investment into a truly game changing Future Transport strategy which will bring together several modes and cutting edge technologies to deliver satisfaction and safety for our customers while supporting a rapidly growing economy.      Advanced Analytics & Insights  We are a trusted partner to our clients, within Customer Strategy and Technology, developing and delivering smart, integrated and sustainable data and analytics solutions which enable evidence-driven decisions to benefit our customers and communities, and leading an uplift in data literacy of use of data insights across the cluster.    The opportunity We have an opportunity for a Senior Data Scientist role to be an integral part of the Advanced Analytics & Insights team within Customer Strategy and Technology. This role will work as a member of a discreet team of data scientists responsible for determining and acting on opportunities to improve the way that the Transport network is developed and managed and customer experience and journeys are continuously improved. Through the intelligent processing and modelling of vast amounts of data, you will develop actionable recommendations that will result in tangible improvements to the services provided by Transport for NSW. What you will be involved in Partner with colleagues to produce statistical analysis and algorithms that support predictive analytics to facilitate improved communication and decision making on the ‘big opportunities’ to ease network congestion, improve safety, and improve the customer journey experience Apply data science techniques using cloud technologies and analytical applications to deliver insights and create new ways of segmenting and managing behaviour of our customers. Work with colleagues, other transport Divisions, contractors, and 3rd parties to identify new data sources that contribute to the delivery of actionable insights. Create features using data science techniques that can be used in reporting, modelling and other analytics applications, ensuring that they are production ready for implementation Create processes for anomaly detection and apply state of the art data mining techniques to large datasets, including public data, to uncover customer sentiment, preferences and behaviours that can be used to inform nudge tactics for mode shift, demand management and utilisation of places Create data assets that assist Transport for NSW in engaging with customers and industry with information that illustrates the benefits of changes to customer behaviour or planning decisions Communicate and engage with stakeholders to collect requirements and communicate insights to improve understanding of factors impacting network performance. About you To be successful in the role you will be:You will have degree qualifications in Data Science, Computer Science, Engineering, or Statistics. Understanding of machine learning & artificial intelligence techniques Expert level skills and experience using SQL to perform analysis and manipulate data efficiently and knowledge of relational databases and architecture. Exposure to data visualisation applications such as Tableau or AWS QuickSight Experience with Big Data platforms and associated applications, including an understanding of NoSQL databases and knowledge and experience using Advanced Analytics applications (Python, R) Good applied statistics skills such as distributions, statistical testing and regression Ability to undertake cross validation of models Experience coordinating with other teams for planning, design, governance, engineering and release management of processes and to ensure timely and accurate delivery of data and analytics services Knowledge and experience building algorithms and applications using advanced scripting and object oriented programming in Python, C# or JAVA. Want to know more?   Please click here to view a copy of the role description.    Interested? Right now is an exciting time to join our team as we deliver an iconic $72.2 billion investment into future transport infrastructure and services over 40 years. Be a part of something big. Apply today to register your interest!   Find out more about Transport for NSW at https://www.transport.nsw.gov.au/about-us.   Our Commitment to Diversity  Great people come from all walks of life. At Transport for NSW, we are committed to creating a diverse, inclusive and flexible workforce which reflects the community and the customers we serve. We actively promote gender diversity in our workplaces, the employment of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders and the employment of people with a disability. We welcome and encourage applications from all people regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, cultural background, or sexual orientation. If you need an adjustment in the recruitment process, please call/text or email the contact person for this role. Salary and Benefits  The salary for this position is TfNSW Grade 9 ($135,898.00 - $152,304.00) per annum plus superannuation and leave loading.   For more information on Employee Benefits at TfNSW please click here.  How to apply  To apply for this position, please submit a resume and address the questions within the application. Need help?   For more information on how to apply for a role in the NSW Public Sector please click here.   For any enquiries, please contact Paul Hollington at  Paul.

title: Senior Data Scientist - Credit Risk
description: Toyota Finance Australia is the country's largest automotive financier. With over 30 years’ experience in the Australian market, an extensive network of regional offices and as a leader within the worldwide business group, we pride ourselves in understanding and listening to our guests. Our unique culture, work approach and business practices make Toyota a successful, global company. We are about more than vehicles and vehicle finance – we are about achieving success in business the ‘right way’ through The Toyota Way philosophy, while continuing to support people and their communities. Our commitment to Continuous Improvement and Respect for People mean our people support each other’s development and success to deliver our global vision of mobility for all. Our Risk Management department located in St Leonards is currently seeking to appoint a Senior Data Scientist on 24-month fixed term full-time basis. Your responsibilities will include:Lead the model development projects on credit scoring, IFRS9 models, loss prediction and other modelling techniques to enhance credit decision making as well as optimize collections and recovery activities. Manage and maintain the current credit risk model such as acquisition scorecards, collection models, credit risk factor models (i.e., PD, LGD, EAD). Provide analytical expertise and support by participating Multi bureau and CCR projects. Maintain effective relationships with internal parties that interact with Data Science teams and Data/System teams, through leading the deliverables on business solution initiatives. Contribute to the Financial planning processes e.g. loss & IFRS9 compliant reserve forecasting, recovery forecasting, capacity planning etc. Partnering with Credit Risk Teams to support credit strategies through account level performance-based analytics and design of appropriate champion/challenger tests as well as preparing policy options/changes/recommendations based on analytics and/or regulatory requirements. Partnering with Enterprise Risk on Risk Appetite Frameworks, KRIs and Stress Testing of the portfolio Partnering with key stakeholders such as regional lending teams, dealer sales Head Office, strategic planning, compliance etc. to drive improvements in business process. Providing analytical expertise and support by participating in cross functional Kaizen activities and contribute feedback and recommendations for continuous improvement and efficiency. To ensure your success in this role, ideally you will have:A degree in quantitative disciplines such as statistics, actuarial science, etc. Over 5 years’ experience in quantitative reporting, analysis, or modelling. Strong analytical skills, experience in business use of statistics is a pre-requisite as is strong working knowledge of SAS, SQL, Excel. (R and Python are advantageous) Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, able to articulate complex analytical information. Ability to maintain high standards of accuracy and work under pressure to achieve deadlines. If you’re keen to join an organisation that recognises the value you add to our business and this is the role you've been looking for, we'd love to hear from you.

description:

We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.
The Fisheries, Aquaculture and Marine Ecosystems (FAME) Division includes the Oceanic Fisheries Programme (OFP) and Coastal Fisheries Programme (CFP). The goal of the OFP is to ensure fisheries that exploit the region’s resources of tuna, billfish and related species are managed for economic and ecological sustainability using the best available scientific information. In pursuing this goal, the OFP provides scientific support for the management of fisheries for tuna and associated species, with a strong focus on stock assessment and modelling, fisheries and ecosystem monitoring and analysis and data management. The OFP works closely with member countries and territories, the Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission, the Forum Fisheries Agency, the Parties to the Nauru Agreement and other regional and sub-regional entities. The role –The Senior Data Scientist / Biometrician – will undertake a programme of work that supports the fisheries and ecosystem monitoring and analysis objectives in the FAME Business Plan. It will undertake analyses to support regional analyses to understand the impacts of fishing and changing climate regimes on the dynamics of tuna populations and their ecosystems in the western and central Pacific Ocean. The key responsibilities of the role include the following: 1. Enhance data analysis services for fisheries & marine ecosystemsData acquisition, management and dissemination, including processing, auditing and consolidating data holdings. Develop systems, tools and support services for standardised data collection, analyses, management and reporting.2. title: Research Associate/Data Scientist
description:
The Ingham Institute for Applied Medical Research (the Institute) is a not-for-profit organisation located in Sydney’s South West that conducts world-class medical research that is rooted in and driven by the needs of the local community and wider Australia.
The Institute is the pre-eminent research institute for South Western Sydney. It is home to 360 staff, over 40 research groups, and five (5) research streams that are committed to its vision of Inspiring Health and Transforming Care.
The Institute is integral to a unique collaboration with the South Western Sydney Local Health District, Western Sydney University and the UNSW Sydney. Through these collaborations the Ingham Institute is working to radically transform health outcomes both locally and globally.
BestSTART is a multidisciplinary translational research team working across the Ingham Institute, Liverpool Hospital, and the main campus in Kensington, Randwick, with a vision of working with the community to facilitate integrated clinical and research activities, ensuring the right level of care for the children of South West Sydney at the right place and the right time. The Women’s Health Initiative Translational Unit (WHITU) comprises clinicians, midwives, scientists, and allied health professionals who share a common goal to improve women’s health through medical research. WHITU’s primary objective is to create an internationally recognised women’s health centre that holistically maximises women’s health and well-being.
The South Western Emergency Research Institute (SWERI) is a unique research entity based at the Ingham Institute at Liverpool Hospital, and carries out research in clinical epidemiology using data linkage and predictive modelling, the impact of multiculturalism on emergency medicine, early diagnosis of critical illness, and innovative patient monitoring.
The Ingham Institute is seeking an experienced Research Associate/Data Scientist to join our team of researchers and clinicians working collaboratively with BestSTART-SWS, WHITU and SWERI.

maintain accurate database and records, take a lead role in data analysis and interpretation, and liaise with researchers and Chief InvestigatorsAssist with the preparation of ethics applications, grant applications, abstracts, annual and progress reports and research outputs, including reports and manuscripts, for publication in high impact journals and correspond with ethics and research governance officers as requiredCollaborate and maintain relationships with researchers and stakeholders associated with the projects and research groups,To be successful in the role you will possess the following:PhD involving big data/a post graduate degree in epidemiology/statistics, computer or related discipline, or appropriate level of expertise gainedCompetency in a range of object-orientated/object function scripting and statistical software, preferably Python/R, and SAS/StataCompetency and experience in undertaking biostatistical analyses of health or similar dataWorking SQL knowledge and experience working with relational databasesStrong organisational skills and ability to work independently with minimal guidanceExperience supporting and working with cross-functional teams in a dynamic environmentExcellent interpersonal skills and the ability to communicate effectively with a variety of internal and external stakeholders from diverse backgrounds and levels of seniorityProven high level organisational skills including the ability to establish priorities, time management, with excellent attention to detailA high level of attention to detail is required for many of the roles responsibilities including data-checking, designing study materials, and organising educational/training/knowledge exchange eventsKnowledge of health and safety responsibilities and commitment to attending relevant health and safety trainingDesirable knowledge and skills:Experience in NoSQL databases particularly Elasticsearch and the ELK stack.
Working knowledge of message queuing, stream processing, and highly scalable ‘big data’ data stores.
Experience in Cerner Command Language / Cerner systems.
Experience using the following software / toolsBig data tools: Hadoop, Spark, Kafka, etc.
Relational SQL and NoSQL databasesData pipeline and workflow management tools: e.g. Airflow.
Stream-processing systems: Storm, Spark-Streaming, etc.

title: Data Scientist
description:
­­­School of Veterinary Science
Founded in 1936, the School of Veterinary Science has a rich history and a reputation for graduating self-reliant, independent and highly capable veterinarians with plenty of initiative and drive. The School has high quality facilities at the UQ Gatton Campus, providing the teaching, research and clinical infrastructure and resources to develop its strong reputation as a leading provider of veterinary training, research and clinical care. The school also maintains a Small Animal Hospital and Large Animal Clinic at Dayboro, north-west of Brisbane.
UQ SpatialEpiLab
The UQ SpatialEpiLab is a One Health medical geography research group based at the School of Veterinary Science established in 2015. The UQ SpatiaEpiLab currently houses +20 staff and research students with a focus on big-data and spatial infectious disease and animal cancer surveillance projects. With a diversity of backgrounds and perspectives, the staff and students at the UQ SpatialEpiLab have broad expertise in health sciences, mathematical modelling, social sciences, ecology and epidemiology. With the support of federal and industry-led projects the UQ Spatial Epidemiology Laboratory is establishing the One Health Surveillance and Analytics Research Unit (OHSARK unit) to conduct research at the interface between animal and human public health. We work with a range of international partners to blend our multidisciplinary expertise and deliver in-depth investigations for many important pathogens around the world. Information about the UQ Spatial Epidemiology Laboratory may be accessed at http://www.spatialepilab.com.
About This Opportunity
OHSARK is building a cloud-native software and platforms to streamline data processing and analysis of human and animal disease data. This is a great opportunity for an experienced Data Scientist to provide support for building and utilising OHSARK’s resulting digital research platforms by supporting the generation of the underlying analysis pipelines. In the role, you will work to engineer raw data into analysis-ready format and deploy statistical and machine learning models in the cloud to support epidemiological visualisations and investigations. This exciting opportunity will have you working alongside the Business Analyst, Senior Software Engineer, and domain scientists across partner institutes and collaboratively funded projects.
For a full list of duties and responsibilities, please refer to the Position Description below.
This position is located at The University of Queensland’s picturesque Gatton Campus. Gatton Campus, UQ combines its Queensland Agricultural College heritage with modern research and teaching facilities in agriculture, agribusiness and veterinary science. Just over an hour’s drive west of Brisbane and five kilometres from the local township, the 1068-hectare Gatton campus offers a relaxed, friendly atmosphere and world-class facilities including the Queensland Animal Science Precinct, the UQ Veterinary Medical Centre, Gatton Research Dairy, nursery and glasshouse facilities, the southern hemisphere’s largest PV solar array research facility, and a pesticide wind tunnel facility. The campus also operates several commercial plant and animal production units in rural technologies to support teaching, research and hands-on training.
Our Ideal Candidate
Applicants must have a degree qualification in a relevant discipline such as health, ecology, statistics, or epidemiology. You will demonstrate strong quantitative reasoning, problem solving and analytical skills, with experience with time-series analysis and/or spatial analysis models. You will have demonstrated research-level data analysis and unit testing experience using C++, Python and/or R. Experience in software version control such as GIT will also set you up for success in this role. Our ideal candidate will also have excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines.
Experience developing data visualization dashboards and deploying multi-core models on high performance computing clusters is highly regarded, but not essential.
You must have ongoing unrestricted work rights in Australia to apply for this opportunity.
The University of Queensland values diversity and inclusion and actively encourages applications from those who bring diversity to the University. Please refer to the University’s Diversity and Inclusion webpage (https://staff.uq.edu.au/information-and-services/human-resources/diversity) for further information and points of contact if you require additional support. Accessibility requirements and/or adjustments can be directed to the contact person listed in the job advertisement.
What We Can Offer
This is a full-time, fixed term position until December 2023 at HEW Level 5.
The remuneration will be in the range of $70,796.58 - $78,852.96, plus employer superannuation of 17%. The total FTE package will be in the range of $82,831.99 - $92.257.96.
You will be able to take advantage of UQ Sport Facilities, salary sacrificing options, on-campus childcare, discounted private health insurance, free parking, discounted veterinary access, development programs and many other benefits.
For further information, please review The University of Queensland's Enterprise Bargaining Agreement 2018-2021

title: Data Scientist
description:
­­­School of Veterinary Science
Founded in 1936, the School of Veterinary Science has a rich history and a reputation for graduating self-reliant, independent and highly capable veterinarians with plenty of initiative and drive. The School has high quality facilities at the UQ Gatton Campus, providing the teaching, research and clinical infrastructure and resources to develop its strong reputation as a leading provider of veterinary training, research and clinical care. The school also maintains a Small Animal Hospital and Large Animal Clinic at Dayboro, north-west of Brisbane.
UQ SpatialEpiLab
The UQ SpatialEpiLab is a One Health medical geography research group based at the School of Veterinary Science established in 2015. The UQ SpatiaEpiLab currently houses +20 staff and research students with a focus on big-data and spatial infectious disease and animal cancer surveillance projects. With a diversity of backgrounds and perspectives, the staff and students at the UQ SpatialEpiLab have broad expertise in health sciences, mathematical modelling, social sciences, ecology and epidemiology. With the support of federal and industry-led projects the UQ Spatial Epidemiology Laboratory is establishing the One Health Surveillance and Analytics Research Unit (OHSARK unit) to conduct research at the interface between animal and human public health. We work with a range of international partners to blend our multidisciplinary expertise and deliver in-depth investigations for many important pathogens around the world. Information about the UQ Spatial Epidemiology Laboratory may be accessed at http://www.spatialepilab.com.
About This Opportunity
OHSARK is building a cloud-native software and platforms to streamline data processing and analysis of human and animal disease data. This is a great opportunity for an experienced Data Scientist to provide support for building and utilising OHSARK’s resulting digital research platforms by supporting the generation of the underlying analysis pipelines. In the role, you will work to engineer raw data into analysis-ready format and deploy statistical and machine learning models in the cloud to support epidemiological visualisations and investigations. This exciting opportunity will have you working alongside the Business Analyst, Senior Software Engineer, and domain scientists across partner institutes and collaboratively funded projects.
For a full list of duties and responsibilities, please refer to the Position Description below.
This position is located at The University of Queensland’s picturesque Gatton Campus. Gatton Campus, UQ combines its Queensland Agricultural College heritage with modern research and teaching facilities in agriculture, agribusiness and veterinary science. Just over an hour’s drive west of Brisbane and five kilometres from the local township, the 1068-hectare Gatton campus offers a relaxed, friendly atmosphere and world-class facilities including the Queensland Animal Science Precinct, the UQ Veterinary Medical Centre, Gatton Research Dairy, nursery and glasshouse facilities, the southern hemisphere’s largest PV solar array research facility, and a pesticide wind tunnel facility. The campus also operates several commercial plant and animal production units in rural technologies to support teaching, research and hands-on training.
Our Ideal Candidate
Applicants must have a degree qualification in a relevant discipline such as health, ecology, statistics, or epidemiology. You will demonstrate strong quantitative reasoning, problem solving and analytical skills, with experience with time-series analysis and/or spatial analysis models. You will have demonstrated research-level data analysis and unit testing experience using C++, Python and/or R. Experience in software version control such as GIT will also set you up for success in this role. Our ideal candidate will also have excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines.
Experience developing data visualization dashboards and deploying multi-core models on high performance computing clusters is highly regarded, but not essential.
You must have ongoing unrestricted work rights in Australia to apply for this opportunity.
The University of Queensland values diversity and inclusion and actively encourages applications from those who bring diversity to the University. Please refer to the University’s Diversity and Inclusion webpage (https://staff.uq.edu.au/information-and-services/human-resources/diversity) for further information and points of contact if you require additional support. Accessibility requirements and/or adjustments can be directed to the contact person listed in the job advertisement.
What We Can Offer
This is a full-time, fixed term position until December 2023 at HEW Level 5.
The remuneration will be in the range of $70,796.58 - $78,852.96, plus employer superannuation of 17%. The total FTE package will be in the range of $82,831.99 - $92.257.96.
You will be able to take advantage of UQ Sport Facilities, salary sacrificing options, on-campus childcare, discounted private health insurance, free parking, discounted veterinary access, development programs and many other benefits.
For further information, please review The University of Queensland's Enterprise Bargaining Agreement 2018-2021

We want to create an earth where infrastructure assets actively identify and communicate problems, converting maintenance liabilities into data-generating assets. We are on a mission to accelerate the world’s transition to safe, intelligent infrastructure. We are a 2-year old Townsville IoT company that is developing technology for the electrical and utilities industries and smart cities. Our LiXiA PUK is an IoT device which attaches to utility poles to measure and infer important parameters including the structural health of poles in near real-time. For asset owners, the technology is focused on enabling predictive maintenance, a self-diagnosing network in real-time, and live data for cross-industry assistance. For Governments and communities, bushfire alerts are an application of ongoing research. Our solutions are manufactured in Townsville, Queensland, for worldwide use. We are looking for a highly energized Data Scientist/Engineer to join our product design and R&D team with strong creative data analytics and visualisation skills. You will be working in a lean and highly skilled team of engineers, scientists, and production technicians. Lixia is a start-up and whilst we energetically work towards developing commercial Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and Data products, we are mindfully defining and establishing a sound engineering platform appropriate for growth. You will be valued for your technical acumen, creative, perseverant, and novel problem-solving skills as well as your positive, collaborative, and autonomous attitude. We are looking for an enthusiastic team member who is well suited to our professional but fun culture.
What you will be doing:Designing and deploying core data infrastructure to support fleets of IIoT devices; managing, optimizing as our data sets grow and our customers, business and product needs matureAnalysing multi-variable data from IIoT device fused with alternate data sets to learn insights and develop novel data products, and assist in focusing our design and R&D teamsOwning major parts of the system, designing, and delivering quality stable solutionsSet-up and maintenance of error logging and data health check processesCollaborating as part of a cross-functional agile teamWhat you will bring:Ideally, 3+ years’ experience working in a technical data role; however, early career professionals are encouraged to also apply Proficiency with Python and RFamiliarity with back end and client facing visualization toolsStrong event driven data experience and the curiosity to validate and verify algorithms A demonstrable ability to implement, maintain and manage databases and data warehouses Understanding of DevOps principles and processesAbility to work with others to design and architect data solutionsA passion for data governanceA strong grasp on best practice and the ability to build, guide and mentor other members on the teamA passion for building automated, fault tolerant and reliable data solutionsA “you build it, you own it” mentalityThe ability to work productively as part of an agile teamA desire to continually improve the way in that you and your teamworkThe ability to communicate clearly and effectively with your team, managers, and stakeholdersIf you cannot bring all the above skills, we are happy to consider capable people with the capacity to pick up missing skills quickly! At Bunnings we believe home improvement should be accessible to everyone. When it comes to working with us, the same applies. Whether you've mastered D.I.Y. or not, you may just be able to find a role that's made for you.

To create a work environment where our team members feel like they belong, we do our best to nurture a supportive culture. Our trust in each other gives us confidence to make an impact in our roles and to our customers.
Our team members are encouraged to lead their own way. Our teams are empowered and encouraged to be accountable for making an impact, no matter how big or small. We are looking for an experienced Data Scientist to join our growing Data & Analytics team.
About the role As the Data Scientist you will be responsible for focusing on delivering business insights, advanced analytics and modelling. The Data Scientist works with complex data sets and understands connections between data points to deliver high quality insights to the business.
Reporting to the Data Scientist Lead, you will develop a deep understanding of the business and work with leaders across Bunnings (Merchandising, Marketing, Logistics, Finance etc.) to understand key strategic issues, identify opportunities and deliver actionable insights. As part of a team, the role encourages and promotes knowledge sharing and learning. Technical expertise in sourcing, manipulating and drawing meaningful insights from disparate datasets is required. Knowledge of key statistical and machine learning techniques is essential along with a demonstrated ability to understand business priorities and then undertaking analysis to identify opportunities and driving business growth. In addition to technical skills, the role also requires strong interpersonal and relationship building skills,embracing the Bunnings culture and possessing a strong commitment to excellent internal and externalcustomer service.
As a Data Scientist you will:Extract insights from disparate data sources utilising a variety of analytical tools and techniquesTurn Data into Insights through:Data Wrangling and Visualisation thus delivering actionable insights to drive business solutions.
Developing and interpreting complex data and information and deliver to stakeholders in a simplified and easy to understand format.
Extract business requirements, objectives & opportunities for stakeholders using your in-depth practical & conceptual knowledge of analytics tools and statistical analysis methods.
Utilise your knowledge and skills in R and/or Python and utilise your specialist technical experience/skills to clean, prepare, manipulate and extract insights from structured datasets, specifically SQL and be able to utilise BI tools to analyse datasets and present insights such as Power
BI. About you You are a detail oriented, flexible, adaptable, problem solver who is forward thinking and lateral in their approach to work with strong analytical, conceptual and collaboration skills. You will have a deep understanding of the key building blocks of data strategy, for example an understanding of the role of the data layer and how data is collected, stored and accessed. You possess excellent analytical and programming skills required to conduct sound data science and be a master of telling compelling stories with data.
You will also have:6+ years working experience in an analytical function, or 3+ years' experience with appropriate academic qualifications.
Direct experience with key analytical platforms that includes Primary: Advanced Analytics (e.g. data science, statistics, machine learning). R and/or Python. Database manipulation (SQL) on technologies including Teradata, Snowflake etc, BI tools (e.g. Power BI) Secondary: Digital tools such as Google Analytics. Cloud platforms (e.g. Azure). Distributed Computing (e.g. Spark) What's in it for you:Competitive salary packageTeam member and partner discountThe opportunity to participate in the Wesfarmers Share PlanAccess to discounted offers from corporate partners12 weeks paid parental leave for eligible team membersOngoing career development and trainingWork in a fun and informal teamA flexible and inclusive work environmentChances to create a real difference in your community and environmentExternal Agencies please note: We request you do not reach out or send unsolicited resumes to HR or any Hiring Managers within the business. title: Health Data Scientist or Early Career Health Data Scientist
description:
Who we are? The Murdoch Children’s Research Institute (MCRI) is home to significant scientific discoveries. We believe there is an answer, a cure or a better treatment for every childhood condition and we’re determined to find it. We are a diverse team of world-leading researchers, doctors, engineers, and hardworking professionals in corporate and scientific services from all corners of the world with one shared goal to transform child health worldwide. Our strength lies in our partnership and co-location with The Royal Children’s Hospital and the University of Melbourne the Melbourne Children’s Campus. This rare model amplifies opportunities to quickly translate research into clinical care. At MCRI, you’ll also find our subsidiary organisation, the Victorian Clinical Genetics Services (VCGS), a specialist childhood, prenatal and adult genetics service. VCGS provides an integrated genetic consultation, counselling, testing and diagnostic support service to children, adults, families and prospective parents. Together, we share a powerful vision: re-imagine the future of child health. Your Opportunity: We are seeking a Health Data Scientist or Early Career Health Data Scientist to join our Centre for Health Analytics team and be responsible for the design, development, validation, and support of technical solutions for a range of clinical data science problems that are being managed by the Centre. The Health Data Scientist or Early Career Health Data Scientist will be responsible for processes and tasks associated with the extraction, transformation, analysis and presentation of health data from the Parkville Electronic Medical Record (EMR) and other RCH information systems. The technical aspects of the role will include the development, validation and troubleshooting of complex and performant SQL queries of health data, then the quantitative analysis and visualisation of extracted data using open source and commercial software. The role will also support the development and implementation of a health data access and analysis platform. Both the Health Data Scientist and Early Career Health Data Scientist will report to the Lead Health Informatician and will include additional opportunities for training and development. Your responsibilities include but are not limited to: Working with the Centre for Health Analytics team to complete health data extracts and analysis requests that achieve the goals of the Centre. Working with stakeholders and other members of the team to analyse health data problems and then design and document requirements for solutions. In partnership with stakeholders, complete quantitative data analyses using open source and commercial software. These data analyses may include exploratory, descriptive, hypothesis tests or predictive analytics. Reviewing and optimising SQL queries to increase performance or reduce impacts of queries on database servers. Maintaining strong working relationships with the internal and external stakeholders to participate in a coordinated support model for the Centre for Health Analytics. Contributing to a positive and supportive work environment for all Centre for Health Analytics team members. Contributing to the continuous improvement of health data and analytical products from the Centre for Health Analytics.

Demonstrated ability to gather and document user requirements. Knowledge of, and skills using, data science software such as R, Python, Julia, Stata, SPSS, or SAS. Interpersonal skills with particular emphasis on gaining consensus, facilitation, and consultation. Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion.
Essential Selection Criteria for Health Data Scientist Highly developed and adaptable analytical and problem-solving skills within a complex data environment. Significant experience in the design, implementation, validation and documentation of data extraction and data transformation processes from an SQL-based information system. Demonstrated ability to build and maintain key working relationships across organisations to ensure a high level of service to customers.
Essential Selection Criteria for an Early Career Health Data Scientist Adaptable analytical and problem-solving skills within a complex data environment. Experience in the design, implementation, validation and documentation of data extraction and data transformation processes from an SQL-based information system. Ability to build and maintain key working relationships across organisations to ensure a high level of service to customers.
Preferred Selection Criteria for Both Roles A post-graduate qualification in computer science, data science, statistics or equivalent. Experience working with health data or health information systems within a hospital, government or private organisation. Certifications or demonstrated experience in Microsoft data technologies (SQL Server, SSMS, SSRS, SSIS, Power Platform). Knowledge and experience with: machine learning methods (such as natural language processing), or research methods (such as experimental design and biostatistical analysis). What’s in it for you: 1 Year Full -Time Contract (Possible Extension). Attractive Salary $89,669 – $107,101 per annum + Super + Salary packaging. Well Being Program and much more. Being part of a happy team of people who like what they do and are passionate about making a difference.

title: Data Scientist, Risk Analytics & Reporting
description:
Rabobank is the world's leading specialist in food and agribusiness banking. title: Assistant Directors: Data Scientist, Data Analyst and Data Manager
description:
The RoleAs an Assistant Director, you will:Lead a section, allocating and prioritising tasks;Be responsible for accurate completion of work within timeframes; andAs an expert in your field, you will design, exploit and implement solutions for data related issues, using new technologies and opportunities. Position 1: Assistant Director - Data Science and Engineering – Data Scientist:Leveraging your experience in Machine Learning/Artificial Intelligence (ML/AI), data analysis and automation, your leadership will assist AGO to derive deeper insights from larger volumes of data at a pace that enables decision advantage. You will liaise with a range of stakeholders to evaluate and implement ML/AI technologies that drive innovation and modernise AGO’s analytic practices.
Position 2: Assistant Director - Data Analytics and Methodologies – Data Analyst:Leveraging your understanding and experience in Geospatial Information Systems (GIS) and scripting languages (such as python), you will work with AGO’s data scientists and capability managers to develop and implement new tools and methodologies that use AGO’s data and GIS more effectively and efficiently. You will work with a range of stakeholders, and coach staff within your team and across the organisation, to increase their digital and data fluency, and enable and empower AGO to work smarter with data.
Position 3: Assistant Director – Geospatial Data Acquisition – Data Manager:In this role, you will mentor a team of geospatial data and commonwealth procurement specialists to ensure requirements are met in an effective, timely and compliant manner. You will lead the development of data requirements with a broad range of stakeholders, and be responsible for delivering those requirements. You will engage broadly with industry to build relationships and drive the best outcomes for AGO. This role also provides the opportunity for the successful candidate to build the team, further refine its functional roles and responsibilities, implement new processes and initiatives, and develop proposals for future the strategic direction of the team.
About our TeamPosition 1: Assistant Director - Data Science and Engineering – Data Scientist:You will lead a small team of data scientists within AGO’s Data Innovation and Analytics Directorate. Your team’s core function is to drive the application of data science to AGO’s analytic problems. This will involve investigating and advising how AGO can create algorithms and machine learning models, develop analytic tools and design data modelling processes, in order to extract and analyse large amounts of structured and unstructured data. You will mentor your team of data scientists to develop their data skills; work closely with a range of stakeholders to understand their analytic requirements; and liaise with capability managers to deliver new tools and methodologies; in order to use AGO’s data more effectively and efficiently.
Position 2: Assistant Director - Data Analytics and Methodologies – Data Analyst: You will lead a small team of data analysts within AGO’s Data Innovation and Analytics Directorate. Your team’s core function is to provide analytical support to AGO’s analytic and production areas, enabling them to achieve outcomes in new and innovative ways. You will mentor your team of data analysts, and work closely with a range of stakeholders to develop their data literacy skills. Your team will develop and implement data analysis tools and methodologies that drive the modernisation and improvement of analytic and production workflows. Your work will enable AGO to provide deeper insights in support of Defence and national intelligence requirements.
Position 3: Assistant Director - Geospatial Data Acquisition – Data Manager:You will lead a team that is helping to shape the strategic direction for Defence’s geospatial data. Your team is responsible for the acquisition of geospatial data from industry partners, and obtaining data from a range sources including domestic and international partners, in order to meet the geospatial data requirements of Defence and the Intelligence community.
Our Ideal CandidateSuccessful candidates will be highly motivated, have strong oral and communication skills, experience leading a team and broad knowledge of geospatial data application and production techniques.
Position 1: Assistant Director - Data Science and Engineering – Data Scientist: You will also have demonstrated data science, machine learning and coding experience and/or qualifications and highly developed analytical, statistical and programming skills with an aptitude for problem-solving. You will also have a broad knowledge of machine-learning and data analysis techniques with experience using popular data science coding languages (such as Python) and data processing frameworks.
Position 2: Assistant Director - Data Analytics and Methodologies – Data Analyst: You will also have demonstrated data science/analytics and coding experience or qualifications, highly developed analytical skills with an aptitude for problem-solving, and broad knowledge of data analysis and automation techniques with experience using GIS applications and scripting languages (such as Python).Position 3: Assistant Director - Geospatial Data Acquisition – Data Manager: You will also have demonstrated experience engaging with industry; and an understanding of, or willingness to learn about, Commonwealth procurement processes.
As the ideal candidate, you will also have:An ability to engage successfully across a range of technical and non-technical stakeholders, both verbally and written;An ability to strategically assess your team’s roles and responsibilities and guide the future direction based on the needs of the Department and broader community;An understanding of Commonwealth procurement processes and industry engagement policies;Highly developed interpersonal and networking skills including experience in negotiation and representation; andAbility to successfully lead and manage a team.
Application Closing Date: Sunday 08 August, 2021For further information please review the job information pack, reference DIG/03209/21 on https://defencecareers.nga.net.au/?jati=7132EF3A-428E-B5F9-A8B1-BFA61B349FB9.

title: Data Scientist
description:
About WorkCover
WorkCover Queensland has been providing workers’ compensation insurance in Queensland for more than 20 years to more than 160,000 businesses.
Supporting Queensland workers and businesses is at the heart of everything we do. The most important thing for us is keeping Queenslanders working and we understand everyone’s needs are different by delivering valued experiences and tailored solutions. Our people are connected to purpose and we’re creating an environment that inspires them to make a difference.
About the role
As an important part of the team, you will work with WorkCover’s comprehensive data assets using innovative statistical, algorithmic, mining and visualisation techniques to find connections and turn them into predictive and prescriptive analytics to support business solutions. With curiosity and deep understanding of our customer, you will be responsible for data cleansing and manipulation and you will influence strategic decisions of management and work with passionate stakeholders across the business. You must be able to clearly articulate your findings and ideas to the wider team.
You will be part of a dynamic team that is made up of technical experts working on multi-million-dollar projects that impact everyday working Queenslanders and support strategic business outcomes. We use programs and tools like SAS programming, R, Qlikview, Tableau, RapidMiner, and Machine Learning algorithms.
About you
The ideal candidate would have:
Tertiary qualifications in Statistics and/or Business
Study in Worker’s Compensation e.g PIEF or related injury schemes
Demonstrated experience (minimum 2 years) in in data analytics/data science including sound knowledge of data wrangling, manipulation and visualization, data modelling, predictive modelling and applied statistics
High proficiency in statistical analysis, quantitative analytics and forecasting/predictive analytics,
Advanced level of expertise in Microsoft Excel, SQL, R/Pythonand and other statistical/analytical/visualization packages (e.g. SAS, Power BI, Qlikview, Tableau, RapidMiner)
Proven ability to proactively use effective interpersonal skills to build and maintain strong and effective relationships with customers, both internal and external
Proven team player with the ability to effectively contribute to achieving team goals, and build mutually rewarding relationships between team members
Ability to prioritise, meet deadlines and achieve established goals and objectives
Superior analytical; and problem solving skills with the ability to apply judgement to make effective decisions

title: Senior Data Scientist
description:
An exciting opportunity for an experienced Senior Data Scientist to create innovative technical solutions that will create value for Suncorp’s customers.
Are you a good communicator who enjoys working with business stakeholders?
Sydney based permanent role
About the role
Suncorp believes in the value and the power of its data to improve its business performance.
The Data Science & AI Centre of Excellence exists to accelerate the value that Suncorp gets from its investments in turning data into tangible value. It does this in two ways:
By developing important use-cases (experiments, prototypes, fully productionised instances) within the team that are integrated into our business processes at scale.
By supporting strategic leaders and the broader data science community across the Suncorp Group to invest in the right initiatives and deliver these utilising best practices. We do this by developing strong business relationships and providing strategic advice to core Data Science & AI decision makers.
The focus of this Senior Data Scientist role is to be one of Suncorp’s leading technical Data Scientists. In this role the successful candidate would have a leading role in designing and delivering technically difficult Data Science and AI initiatives that produce significant business value.
Key Responsibilities
Engage with business stakeholders, understand their pain points and opportunities and work with them to solve their most difficult and impactful problems.
Combine an inquisitive mind with an ability to understand a customer’s business context and translate the understanding into an innovative and iterative data science solution design that delivers value to business unit customers quickly.
Create innovative data science technical solutions that you will execute to create value for our customers.
Be accountable for the design and delivery of complex advanced data science components (data, models, algorithms, advice etc.) using onshore and offshore resources.
Work within an agile framework to deliver incremental value to business customers throughout a project’s lifecycle.
Be accountable for the quality control of the core data science components (data, models, algorithms, advice etc) being delivered to Group customers.
Possess exceptional technical capability in one or more areas of data science/machine learning.
Provide thought leadership on data science and AI ‘best practice’ through ongoing scans of the external environment. This includes the data science and AI ecosystem (e.g. platforms, tools and processes).
Advise other team members (and wider Technology & Transformation and Group team members) on relevant matters.
Skills & Experience:
Superior results in a relevant advanced technical bachelor’s degree in quantitative subject area (e.g. statistics, actuarial, data science, mathematics, computer science).
Membership of relevant professional body (e.g. IAPA, Actuaries’ Institute etc.) is valued, as the successful candidate is expected to be well-connected into external best practice.
Typically, this role requires 7+ years of relevant experience (in an advanced analytical or data science related field of work).
Advanced level of competence in solving difficult problems, using data science (advanced analytical) techniques.
Advanced knowledge of the execution of a wide range of Data Science techniques and being able to do this in a way that is focussed on delivering tangible value. Must have experience in delivering complex machine learning or multivariate predictive analytics solutions in a commercial context (i.e. generalised linear models, tree-based approaches, NLP techniques etc).
Data science platform and engineering knowledge is highly valued.
Proficient communication skills to be able to co-design solutions with customers. Emotional intelligence and the ability to communicate complex ideas to a range of internal stakeholders.
Our Benefits
Discounts of up to 25% on our various Insurance, Banking & Superannuation products
Flexible working environment and arrangements; genuine focus on work-life balance
Numerous discounts with our corporate partners (retail & shopping / travel & holiday / health & wellbeing)

Suncorp is a leading financial services provider in Australia and New Zealand, enabling more than nine million customers to better protect and enhance their financial wellbeing. With a heritage dating back to 1902, we have grown to become a top-50 ASX-listed company with over 13,000 people. title: Snr Data Scientist
description:
Data Scientist:This role sits within the Compliance section of the Business Intelligence team and is at the forefront of creating a data driven compliance program and delivering better digital services. The role would suit someone willing to apply their strong technical skills to manipulate and present data in a way that drives value for the business. A curiosity and a willingness to solve problems is essential to this role. Experience in helping a business design a data driven solution, as opposed to just building from a given plan, is essential.
Key responsibilities:The successful candidate will work as part of a team to understand the needs of the Revenue Office and how our data assets can assist with solving problems and improving processes. To achieve this, candidates will need the following attributes:
• developing algorithms to detect non-compliance with applicable tax laws and present results in a meaningful way.
• finding insight from new and existing data sources and communicating this to the business
• matching data from disparate sources.
• a genuine curiosity about the problems to be solved.
• be more interested in delivering value to the business and seeing the impact of their work, rather than using specific tools and creating complex models.
• be pragmatic, flexible and comfortable with ambiguity and change.
• excellent communication skills, including the ability understand problems by asking questions, inform the business about what solutions can be delivered, and explain these data driven solutions to non technical people.
Essential Selection Criteria:
• Experience working with large, disparate data sets and an ability to extract value from these.
• Programming skills and experience working with statistical analysis tools.
• Demonstrated capacity to develop, plan and deliver results.
• Demonstrated capacity to develop, support and mentor colleagues.
• Excellent communication skills. Relevant professional qualifications/certifications, and/or extensive relevant experience is essentialOnly suitably qualified candidates with Citizenship will be shortlistedResume and short suitability statement in word format please to Dwayne Joyce at djoyce@au.drakeintl.com

title: APS6 Data Analyst, Intelligence & EL1 Senior Data Scientist, Intelligence
advertiser: Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre (AUSTRAC)
description:
About AUSTRAC and what we doCriminals and terrorists are targeting the financial sector, using it to hide and move their illicit wealth, funnel money to illegal business operations and conflicts overseas, or supporting crimes such as drug trafficking, child sex exploitation and terrorist attacks. These crimes impact every Australian, from increasing the cost of living right through to our loved ones being harmed. At AUSTRAC, it’s our job to protect the community by disrupting this activity and prevent it from occurring in the first place. AUSTRAC is the Australian Government’s financial intelligence unit and anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing regulator. With government and industry partners, we use financial intelligence and regulation to: Prevent criminal abuse of the financial sector;help business, government and law enforcement partners detect, deter and disrupt money laundering, terrorism financing and other serious crimes;build and maintain trust and integrity in Australia’s financial system. Every day our people use their intellect, skills, initiative and the latest technologies to protect our country, economy and community.
Our purpose is to build resilience in the financial system and use financial intelligence and regulation to disrupt money laundering, terrorism financing and other serious crime.
The Intelligence Division The Intelligence Division oversees the intelligence operations of AUSTRAC, and is Australia’s Financial Intelligence Unit. Intelligence Division is also responsible for Fintel Alliance—the AUSTRAC-led Public Private Partnership—and AUSTRAC’s engagement with international partners. Current vacancies and locationsAUSTRAC currently has multiple APS6 Data Analysts and EL1 Senior Data Scientists vacancies across the Intelligence Division in Sydney, Melbourne and Canberra.
We are seeking highly motivated individuals who can contribute to maintaining a high performance culture and supporting the delivery of financial data within our Intelligence Division. With supportive benefits and culture, we offer a challenging and rewarding career where you can make a real impact. A career at AUSTRAC will open the door to a vast range of future opportunities domestically and internationally. Merit pools may be established and used to fill future vacancies within the next 12 months. More information and How to ApplyOur website: https://www.austrac.gov.au/How to Apply: https://www.austrac.gov.au/careers/current-vacancies“Come and join the fight against financial crime”
