title: Data Scientist
description:
Working for AMP
Working for AMP means being part of a company that values diverse thinking, encourages collaboration and promotes innovation. It’s an environment that offers challenging and exciting work as well as opportunities for professional growth. We’re flexible enough to allow you to make the most of your life, both professionally and personally.
We are looking for those that have the courage and agility to navigate changing and complex environments so that we can deliver the best solutions for our customers. We value people with integrity, an innate willingness to help others and an eagerness to perform to the best of their abilities.
We’re transforming our business, and we need people like you to join us on this journey.
About the role
The Chief Operating Officer (COO) function is the technical, operational, and project delivery hub of AMP, partnering with AMP business units to design, deliver and manage innovative technology and operational solutions that meet the current and future needs of customers. Our vision is to be recognised as AMP's technology innovators and integrators, applying world-class best practice standards and processes within AMP’s operations.
The Data Analytics team is responsible for implementation of data integration & maintain cloud data infrastructure. The team is also responsible for the data governance, standardizing the delivery process and performing the value-add services such as automation, providing best practices, defining on-boarding process.
We are looking for a proven, capable and reliable Data Scientist with good communication skills and the ability to work in an Agile environment and work collaboratively with a stable team. You should also want to work with the latest tech stack. The core focus will be on Scala and Spark (along with a background in Java) and ideally with some experience working on the AWS platform.
Key responsibilities
Support development of business cases by coordinating estimates for the development team
Work with Portfolio Managers to establish team priorities and delivery schedules
Coordinate development resources and contribute to selection of appropriate solutions.
Coordinate the development team and endure best practice principles in software development are applied to solution development
Work with peers at all stages of the SDLC to deliver the best possible outcome for our stakeholders
Build and foster effective relationships with Business and IT teams internally and externally
Work closely with 3rd party suppliers who deliver and manage the application and supporting infrastructure

Capabilities & Experience:
You will expand and optimise our clients’ data and data pipeline architecture, as well as optimise their data flow and collection for cross functional teams.
Experience working with AWS
Hands on experience working with streaming technologies like Kafka, Spark streaming. Etc
Experience working with API Development
Should have knowledge of data science workflows (end to end ML modelling)
Hands on experience working with Hadoop, Spark, Scala, Strong Scala, Python and SQL knowledge
Hands on experience with ETL, Data Ingestion, CI/CD Pipelines, Data Quality, Master and Meta Data Management some experience with visualisation tools such as Tableau or Spotfire.
Build robust, efficient and reliable data pipelines consisting of diverse data sources to ingest and process data into cloud platform.
Should have good stakeholder management and communications skills will allow you to successfully keep the team updated on deliverables and ensure key project stakeholders are aware of progress against project milestones.
Experience working with different business units to support the execution of machine learning, AI and analytics to solve real-world business problems.
Provide thought leadership in support of design and implementation of a big-data platform. Lead in the transformation from structured to unstructured data, evaluating new technologies and approaches leading to scalable Big Data platforms.
Qualifications
Tertiary qualifications in computer science, engineering or other relevant qualification.
Wellbeing & Benefits
As a company that values wellbeing, we offer a range of great benefits to support you financially, professionally and personally. These include access to a wide range of flexible working options including the ability to purchase extra leave, retail discounts, onsite wellbeing centre including a gym (Sydney Office), Employee Assistance Program, competitive home loan rates, leading superannuation contribution, discounted financial advice and personal insurance.
Inclusion & Diversity
AMP recognises individual differences and welcomes people from a variety of life and work experiences. The diversity of our people is core to our ability to innovate, grow and to fulfil our collective aspiration of helping people to own their tomorrow. A natural curiosity, a respect for differences and a growth mindset are valued at AMP.

title: Data Scientist
description:
Do you want to join a conscious & innovative green-tech start-up?Do you want to work with passionate people who are excited about solar energy and doing good in the world?Are you a skilled data scientist who enjoys exploring? About Solar AnalyticsSolar Analytics is a successful green-tech start-up that provides solar home energy management for rooftop solar photovoltaic energy systems. Founded in 2011 by a team of passionate, world leading solar experts, we have developed a cloud-based data and analytics platform for solar electricity production and consumption and today we are Australia’s largest independent third-party solar and energy monitoring provider.
Our core values drive everything we do; we put people first, we do meaningful work, we collaborate, we have fun, we are dependable and we explore. We are seeking a like-minded, well-qualified Data Scientist who will have the drive to propose optimisation and improved strategies to achieve new customer values and insights, as well as the overhaul of legacy algorithms, and is eager to be part of a team who is making a real difference.
About The RoleReporting to the CTO, you will be:Working with our team of energy and product engineers to drive our analytical capabilities forward by identifying opportunities for our product to improve; as well as working with our software engineers to help get solutions delivered.
Producing insights from distributed solar production, energy consumption and network quality data generating internal and external valueExtending ML capabilities and team to drive projects related to optimisation of battery and overall home energy usage, as well as solar generation forecasting.
Leading a team of data analysts and PV engineers that focus on uncovering business valueManaging and maintaining the process for procuring high impact datasets for our data product partnersAssisting other staff with technical reports and data for internal and external communicationWorking across all scales of the solar industry, including residential, commercial and industrial, and utility-scaleWhat we are looking forTertiary qualification in science, engineering or computer science or equivalent experienceDemonstrate strengths in data management, preparation, analysis and presentationCommercial exposure to working in Data Science building a range of complex modelsAbility to review existing analytics processes to propose more efficient and accurate alternatives or extensions.
Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skillsAbility to write technical reports and commercial correspondence to verbally convey information in a clear and concise mannerExperience with programming in a production Python environmentExtra consideration:Experience in energy industry, especially photovoltaics or energy marketsExperience with AWS (EC2/Athena/S3), PostgreSQL, Python What we offerA great opportunity to make a real difference to the fastest growing segment of the renewable energy industry;A salary package which will be commensurate with experience and will include bonus plus shares;A benefits package, including, flexible work arrangements, well-being program and professional development;A ‘family-like’ culture with a like-minded team who knows how to have fun along the way. Solar Analytics is committed to workplace diversity. Between us we speak over 15 languages and we employ a large number of pioneering and influential women, many of whom are in leadership roles within our company. Join us to see this in action, not just words. Our office is a vibrant and welcoming workplace; children and pets are regular visitors and most staff work at least half the week from home.
Confidence can sometimes hold us back from applying for a job. However, there is no such thing as a ‘perfect’ candidate. Solar Analytics is a place where everyone can grow. So however you identify and whatever background you bring with you, please apply if this is a role that would make you excited to come into work every day.

title: Data Scientist -  Customer Insights Pharmaceutical Industry
description:
Our client is a leader in the global pharmaceutical market who have won awards for their customer focus and are well respected for what they do. With a strong pipeline of products, they have an ever-changing focus on their customer needs and engagement. This role requires someone with significant skills in data science along with the proven capability to develop actionable insights that create and optimise the customer journey. The Position The role of the data scientist is to work within the Customer Engagement & Insights Business Unit (CEIBU) and across the Prescription Medicine business You will extract, integrate, and analyse data to generate insights to understand and engage with their customers and optimise the customer experience Bring key stakeholders together to answer strategic business questions Create change and insights to ensure business decisions are made based on sound information This role involves the identification, extraction, cleansing, formatting, and integration of disparate data sources and analytics and transform available information streams from their Go-To-Market platforms. Collaborate cross-functionally with other teams and data providers to identify the relevant data needed to create business insights. Create an insights culture and drive the change by facilitating conversations that help to generate insights and regularly present insights based on proactive analysis of business scenarios Present to groups of senior management with strategies based on data analytics that could improve the customer experience The Candidate Experienced data scientist and general marketing analytics expert with experience in extracting and formatting data from digital platforms. Familiar with pharma analytics as well as the nature and design of insightful test and learn scenarios. Independent thinker and subject matter expert. Excellent communication skills and the ability to facilitate discussions with senior management to drive change and communicate insights in business language to a broad range of stakeholders. Advance Excel skills such as data summarisation with Pivot Table, dynamic Data Visualization, Data Query/Connection, and Power Query Editor. Experience with using Data Science programs, such as R, Python and SQL for data preparation and transformation (ETL), run statistical tests and experiments, use Machine Learning models for prediction and segmentation. Bachelor’s Degree in Pharmaceutics / Statistics / Analytics Pharmaceutical industry experience is key, although Banking, Finance, FMCG and Digital Agency industry experience will be considered. Energy, results focus and a high achieving attitude are essential as is the ability to show a passion for what you do The Rewards Full-time permanent position Opportunity to join big pharma and develop a career in a fast moving market segment Substantial career opportunity working with one of the best in the pharmaceutical industry Excellent base salary About US EP HealthcareWhy work with EP Healthcare? We have developed an outstanding network of clients, as well as a very thorough knowledge of the Healthcare industry. How? Because we’ve all worked in it ourselves as reps, managers, marketers - not just recruiters! We support our candidates by offering a personalised and experienced approach, every step of the interviewing process. Click the APPLY button to send your CV.

title: Data Scientist
description:
Are you looking for the next step in your Data Science career? Something that's equally as fresh as it is exciting? Somewhere you can see your contributions come to life? We may have the answer you have been looking for.
We are on the hunt for a highly analytical Data Scientist to join our Data Science team. This role will provide you with heaps of personal growth opportunities, a super workplace culture and the opportunity to get stuck into awesome projects. Reporting directly to the Senior Data Science Manager, this rare opportunity will be responsible for working with Betfair's rich data, as well as external data to create data science driven outputs to drive business value. We are supportive and revel in working together on exciting projects. Where possible, you should support your claims with specific examples of what you have done and how you did it. However you identify, and whatever background you bring with you, please apply if this is a role that would make you excited to come to work every day!

title: Data Scientist
description:
Job Reference: 766001DATA SCIENTISTFaculty of Health – About Us: This position presents an exciting opportunity, in collaboration with the WA Cancer Registry and WA Cancer and Palliative Care Network Clinical Implementation Unit, to make a major impact in the development of the collection of cancer staging information and related epidemiological reports and research. The WA Cancer Registry is the only complete and accurate source of cancer incidence and mortality data for Western Australia since 1982, and plays a vital role in improving outcomes for Western Australian cancer patients by monitoring cancer related trends and survival, supporting research studies, and evaluating cancer prevention and health promotion programs. Cancer stage at diagnosis is the most significant risk factor determining cancer patients' prognosis and is critical in understanding early diagnosis, yet has never been routinely collected at the population level. This project will develop and apply machine learning and natural language processing algorithms to estimate stage at diagnosis and integrate them into the WA Cancer registry processes. This role will develop the collection of cancer staging information and epidemiological research. Your new roleWork with the Lead Data Scientist to develop, apply and validate new or existing machine learning and natural language processing algorithms to derive stage at diagnosis according to cancer type. Work with the Lead Data Scientist to develop software and document the processes required for the optimisation of data pipelines, architectures, schemas and datasets related to the ongoing integration of cancer staging algorithms. Contribute to journal articles and reports relating to the process of capturing, validating and integrating stage at diagnosis derived from the algorithms. Liaise with internal and external stakeholders and collaborators as required to ensure the appropriateness and acceptability of the algorithms developed. As a member of the University community, demonstrate the highest possible standards of professional and personal conduct, modelling the University’s Values and Signature Behaviours. Undertake other activities which the incumbent might reasonably be expected to do, and which are consistent with the accountabilities and responsibilities as listed above. The successful applicant will have (selection criteria): A tertiary qualification in software engineering, computer science, information technology or related discipline with considerable relevant experience or an equivalent combination of relevant experience and/or education/training. Technical Knowledge, Experience and Skills: o Demonstrated ability to work with software development and data analytics across different disciplines. o Knowledge and experience working with relational databases and query authoring (SQL). o Experience building and optimising data pipelines, architectures, schemas and datasets. o Proficiency in at least one analytics scripting language (such as Python, R). Non-technical Knowledge, Experience and Skills: o Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to understand and effectively tackle challenging problems. o Demonstrated ability to work effectively as part of a team as well as autonomously. o Demonstrated ability to articulate complex, technical concepts to non-technical clients and the ability to consult and liaise with personnel. o Demonstrated well developed written communication skills with the ability to construct clear and concise reports and correspondence. Desirable: o Experience working with developing machine learning and natural language processing models. o Experience working with Agile software development methodologies. o Experience working with data relevant to health research and government / health service providers. Apply your creative and innovative thinking to solving complex problems using your data science skills
Pursue your passion for learning and getting things done
Join a mature and highly skilled team
Senior Data Scientist
About the role
The data science team aspires to create value from data through the use of advanced analytics, cognitive computing and AI.
The role of Senior Data Scientist is accountable for creating core data, models and algorithmic components that form part of data science solutions, uplifting the group’s advance analytics capability and provide innovative outcomes to enhance our customer experience.
Some Key Accountabilities
Provide subject matter expertise and possess exceptional technical capability in one or more areas of data science
Participate in and/or lead the design and technical development of data science initiatives (data, models, algorithms advice etc.)
Research, design and build pragmatic, scalable, and statistically rigorous solutions
Engage with business stakeholders understand their pain points, identify opportunities and contribute to developing advanced analytical/data science solutions that can create real value for them
Contribute to the evaluation of possible data sources and analytical techniques that could be used to provide a superior business outcome.
Successful Data Scientist will have:
Technical post graduate qualification (statistics, actuarial, engineering, maths etc) is essential.
A wealth of experience in commercial complex data science/advanced analytics, with a specialist skill set.
Solid proficiency in Python. Highly advantageous: SQL, xnix, stash, bitbucket code management.
Experience in delivering complex multivariate predictive analytics solutions in a commercial context (such as, predictive modelling, text analytics, optimisation and decisioning algorithms). Understanding of digital data and analytical applications in near real time would be highly advantageous.
Highly valued: experience working with clickstream data.
A desire to continually upskill and adapt technical skills to the changing data science technical landscape.
Need to have a curious mind that doesn’t accept the status quo
Superior communication skills
What Suncorp will offer in return:
High potential career development opportunities at an ASX top 20 company on the move
A professional, supportive and friendly culture
A range of corporate and life style benefits
Employer of choice for gender equality

title: Data Scientist
description: OUR STORY We believe it’s time for a new type of bank. One that steps up and does the right thing by its customers; that puts them first. One that is relevant and meaningful in today’s world. We’re that new type of bank. We’re digital only, and harness the capabilities of technology, data and artificial intelligence to deliver an entire bank in the palm of your hand. We exist solely to serve our customers - to give them a smarter, more personalised banking experience. We are constantly adapting and evolving to help customers make better, more informed financial decisions. We do things in real time, to bring real value to their lives. We put them first. And we do this every second, of every minute, of every day. All 86,400 of them. We’re 86 400. YOUR WHY You are excited to play a role in growing a fledgling data science programme and will use your understanding of advanced analytics and statistical modelling to generate insights, refine our product strategy and promote a culture of experimentation and measurement. You’ll like to be close to the action – this role will partially embed with our product and UX teams, and will also collaborate closely with our agile delivery squads to develop triggers and models for customer-facing app features. This role reports to the Head of Data and Analytics. HOW YOU’LL SPEND YOUR TIME AT 86 400 As a Data Scientist you will be expected to: Develop analytics deep dives into customer behaviour and feature utilisation by exploring data from transactional sources, client systems, web analytics and external providers. Confidently present findings and recommendations back to our product and UX/design teams to shape the future of the 86 400 customer experience. Implement an experimentation framework and utilise A/B testing to validate the impact of feature releases across different cohorts and demographics. Focus on improving data literacy across the business, teaching partner teams when, where, and how to harness data to inform decision making. Identify opportunities for the development of advanced analytic algorithms/models that may enhance or extend the 86 400 customer experience. Collaborate with our Data Engineers and delivery teams to develop, train, orchestrate and deploy these assets. Work as part of the Data & Analytics function to uplift shared practices and processes, and to build out our centralised data platform for data science use cases. WHAT MAKES YOU TICK A blank page doesn’t scare you – you focus on solutions even when faced with ambiguity You are a strong communicator, skilled in explaining complex concepts to non-technical audiences and able to tell a compelling story with data. You aren’t afraid to challenge established thinking based on the results of your analysis You know that in practice data science is about more than building ML models, but aren’t afraid to have a go at that if it’s the right solution for the problem You work well autonomously, balancing the demands of partners against larger strategic initiatives, but like the idea of still having a like-minded team to hang out with for Friday drinks You know when to put your hand up for help when stuck, or for guidance on priorities WHAT YOU WILL BRING TO 86 400 Proficient with at least one statistical package/programming tool (Python, R) and a SQL expert Skilled in one or more data visualisation tools (Plotly, PowerBI, Tableau, etc.) Experience in designing and analysing experiments that drive key decisions A strong foundational background in statistics (distributions, probability, inference, etc.) Knowledge of overall process of model pipelines (training, hyperparameter tuning, etc.) Good business planning, analytical and conceptual skills Strong skills with Jira & Confluence and an ability to manage competing deliverables EssentialAt least 5 years practical experience in the analysis of large and complex data sets Experience working with cloud-based data and analytics platforms Ability to visualise and present complex data to non-technical audiences Appropriate tertiary qualification in statistics, data science or an equivalent discipline DesirablePrevious work experience in a financial services or digital product environment Experience implementing A/B testing frameworks and creating tools to track results Previous experience with Databricks for analytics and data science work A good sense of humour VALUES. EVERY SECOND Customer. Customer - We put the customer’s best interests at the forefront of everything we do. We believe financial success will follow customer success. Agile and Brave - Constantly collaborating in new ways to create something genuinely innovative. Value Each Other - We respect everyone’s contribution, embracing a common goal and championing individuality. Frank and Authentic - A high performing team who say what we mean and mean what we say to create a strong team culture. Show Up - We bring our passion, positivity and sense of fun every day to embrace the challenges of changing the banking game. If you are looking to look for an innovative company which adds value, then this is the role for you. A competitive package is on offer for the successful candidate. Visit: www.86400.com.au Please note: no agencies will be accepted in the recruitment of this role. We would like to take this opportunity to thank all candidates for their application. title: Data Scientist
description:
About The RoleJoining our Data Science team, you will play a key role in developing end-to-end data science & ML solutions that will be applied across the entire business: customer behaviour, finance, responsible gambling, fraud identification and risk pricing.
Through developing and refining these models, the Data Science team help create best in market products, deliver tailored experiences to our customers and improve the efficiency and margin of the digital business. The role includes an element of R&D where new and emerging technologies and tools are applied to further extend the business knowledge and understanding of customers and digital wagering markets. As a Data Scientist with our team, your key responsibilities will include:
Develop complex predictive models using advanced statistical and machine learning tools to understand and forecast customer behaviour, business performance, and market condition.
Develop and maintain a detailed understanding of Entain digital wagering products and solutions in order to identify opportunities to improve pricing and targeting models.
Analyse model performance, customer behaviour and market conditions to provide key insights to business stakeholders.
Maintain an understanding of current and emerging trends in quantitative analysis, machine learning and data engineering.
Identify and drive opportunities to apply new approaches or technologies to help build the business.
Present findings to key stakeholders to inform business decisions.
Key Skills and Experience:
A minimum of 12 months experience in a Data Science or similar role.
Strong Python & SQL. Experience with Scala, R, Go, JS/TS is beneficial.
Experience in PowerBI & Dash highly desirable. Experience creating interactive visualisations in other platforms (eg. Spotfire, Tableau) is beneficial.
Knowledge of underlying mathematical foundations of statistics & machine learning.
Experience in MLOps & cloud is highly desirable.
Self-driven with the ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
Experience conveying technical concepts to a non-technical audience.
About us!We’re Entain. Our vision is to be the world leader in sports betting and gaming entertainment. We are creating exciting and trusted experiences for our customers and revolutionising the gambling space as we go. We’re experts in safer gambling and the company that is at the forefront of responsibility.
Combining technology and entertainment to create products that push the boundaries, Entain is home to a global family of more than 25 well-known brands – names such as Ladbrokes Australia, neds, Bookmaker.com.au, betstar, and many more.
Our growth and success have come from driving innovative and market leading betting experiences developed in-house by our exceptional team. With the attitude of a start-up but the support of a significant multi-national company, Entain is an exciting place to work!What's on offer?

title: Data Analyst / Data Scientist
description: Our large Federal Government client is seeking to engage the services of a Data Analyst / Data Scientist for a prominent project with regards to COVID-19. Implementation of the Australian COVID-19 vaccine rollout is of high national priority and visibility. Monitoring the COVID-19 vaccination rollout for different population cohorts can help identify vaccination coverage in priority and vulnerable populations such as those identified by the Australian Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation (ATAGI), thereby assisting in informing targeted public health actions and communications. All vaccines given to people in Australia, including COVID-19 vaccines, are recorded in the Australian Immunisation Register (AIR). Linking AIR data to other government data can provide visibility and insights into vaccine coverage in specific population cohorts. The Multi-Agency Data Integration Project (MADIP) is a partnership among Australian Government agencies to develop a secure and enduring approach for combining nationally important datasets. It incorporates population-level socio-demographic data such as the census, tax data, Medicare and Pharmaceutical data, disability data and more. This project links AIR data to MADIP data to provide population-level insights into COVID-19 vaccine coverage among specific cohorts of interest such as people with disability (PWD), culturally and linguistically diverse (CALD) populations, people in specific occupations (e.g. aged care workers), people with an underlying medical condition and potential low uptake groups. This project will create regularly reporting linked analytical outputs using supplementary high-quality socio-demographic data held in MADIP and AIR. It will also examine a variety of adhoc requests and longer-term research questions, including those related to vaccine effectiveness and safety. Position Key Responsibilities Weekly reporting – updating weekly vaccination coverage reports with refreshed data. Modifying weekly reports in response to evolving priorities and requirements. Ad hoc analysis – using a range of data analytics, data science and data presentation techniques to provide insights in response to ad hoc requests and queries. Requirements aren’t necessarily clear; creativity and strong problem-solving skills are necessary. Producing high quality reports, slide decks, visualisations and dashboards (we use Qlik Sense, but experience using other BI tools is helpful.) Collaborating with a range of stakeholders to refine business requirements. A track record of working well with others is necessary. Ability to deliver high quality work under high pressure with tight timeframes is necessary. Essential criteria Strong conceptual, problem solving, research and analytical skills including interpreting information and data as well as a high level of data modelling skills. Solid written communication skills and capacity to produce high quality policy papers, briefings and reports with attention to detail. High level interpersonal skills, with the ability to establish and maintain strong working relationships with internal and external stakeholders. Ability to work independently with limited guidance, and to prioritise tasks to meet tight deadlines as well as work in a team when required. Demonstrated policy and/or project management skills, including policy and/or project development, implementation, communication and risk management. Experience in Microsoft Excel and/or programming languages for modelling, data analysis (e.g. SAS, R, Python and SQL etc.), and visualisation tools (e.g. Qlik, Tableau, etc.). title: Data Scientist
description:
About UsHoneysuckle Health exists to help people lead healthier lives. We do this by understanding the current and future health needs of individuals, helping them to prevent and manage disease risk and make better treatment decisions. Honeysuckle Health aims to play a leading role in Australia’s healthcare system by engaging customers, medical practitioners, payers and allied health providers in the provision of innovative, evidence-based healthcare services and programs.
Our ability to interpret future healthcare risk, support decision making of individuals and healthcare providers and deliver healthcare interventions improves health outcomes at both an individual and population level. We augment this with providing health consumers and health funders value and outcomes based funding approaches which ensure affordability and drives sustainability in the health-care system.A career at Honeysuckle Health presents a unique and exciting opportunity to provide support to health consumers, health funders and provider in the best possible application of health care services. Being a Data Scientist at Honeysuckle HealthAs a Data Scientist at Honeysuckle Health, you might be:Conducting scientific experiments to determine if a health program is effective.
Training and deploying machine learning models to automatically identify patients that would most benefit from receiving specific health programs.
Optimising health insurers’ networks of preferred practitioners, for best outcomes and cost.
Providing advice on the use of machine learning and statistical techniques.
Presenting findings to internal stakeholders.
We work in partnership with health insurers, so we have access to decades worth of anonymised medical claims data: well enough to measure trends in health improvement. Honeysuckle Health was started in 2020, so we use the latest tools and are fully cloud-based. For our Data Warehouse we’ve picked Snowflake and dbt (Data Build Tool); and for data science work we use Databricks, and a bit of AWS Sagemaker. CriteriaA STEM uni degree with a strong math/stats component, or equivalent industry experience.
Good programming skills: SQL is a must, combined with either R or Python.
Data mining, wrangling and visualisation (using Python, Tableau or AWS QuickSight).Experience designing, running, and analysing experiments (A/B testing, randomised trials).Experience building machine-learning (ML) models.
Desirable:Every patient is different: we’re looking for someone with an eye for potential confounding variables, sources of bias; and the statistical know-how to correct them.
You’ll interact with a wide audience: we’re looking for an ability to communicate your results and explain DS concepts in laymen’s terms: statistical significance, skewed distributions.
While we have Ops, Data Engineers and Analysts, we’d still like you to be familiar with all aspects of a Data Science. In particular: data acquisition automation, design principles of a data warehouse, deployment of ML model on the cloud, and more.
Exposure to a complete project: from gathering a customer’s requirements all the way to delivering a working solution.
The ability to cover the entire speed-vs-quality range: start with fast-turnaround “proof-of-concept" work; then iteratively progress towards a “production grade” implementation.
Familiarity with Git, and Data Science Ops and automation (CI/CD, automated re-training) Benefits Flexible working arrangements (including option to work from home 2 days/week once competent in the role)Employee Private Health Insurance discountShort-term incentive programsEducational assistancePaid parental leaveVolunteer leaveA dynamic and energetic working environmentThe ability to work collaboratively within a team that embraces changeA beautiful office location in the CBD of NewcastleBeing a start-up has some advantages… Diversity of work: expect to build many proof-of-concepts to probe market interest.
We have an Agile mindset.
You’ll never work on outdated or legacy technology, nor on-prem systems! We also tend to buy existing solutions to our problems, instead of reinventing the wheel or building our own. To ApplyPlease apply with a CV and Cover Letter. We recommend your cover letter begin by introducing yourself and explaining why you would like to work as a Data Scientist at Honeysuckle Health. Please also include a section covering a project you’ve worked on: explain the business problem it attempted to address, your role, how you went about solving the problem, who you interacted with, what you’ve learned, and finally the outcomes of the project.
Once these documents are ready, please upload them at the address below. At this stage, be prepared to complete a timed test, comprising of 10 multiple-choice questions that cover Data Science and SQL fundamentals.https://apply.hire.toggl.com/PMRD0Y1V5D9DM5V3HZ52 [link removed]

title: Data Scientists – Address Register
description:
The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) is seeking to recruit Data Scientists at the APS 5 and APS 6 classification levels to work in our Address Register section in either our Melbourne or Canberra offices. The roles can be filled permanently or temporarily, either on a full-time or part-time basis.
The Address Register team manage a critical piece of ABS statistical infrastructure used for list- based survey and Census frames and for data integration. The Address Register also creates geocoding indexes that allow statistical outputs to be spatially coded and visualised using an accurate and up to date set of addresses.
The goal of the team is to provide innovative solutions to keep the Register current by adopting new technology solutions, administrative and big data sources and machine learning techniques. The APS 5 Data Scientist will focus on:implementing geospatial representation of data at large scalecollaborating with methodological and technical experts to design solutions that are future proofed and take advantage of new big data and explore alternate data structuresdesigning solutions to analyse new datasetswrangling, interrogating, and interpreting large datasetsassisting predictive model development using machine learning methods including supervised learning, classification, anomaly detection and feature engineeringquality assuring data outputscontributing to a high performing team.
The APS 6 Data Scientist will focus on:developing new processes and innovative solutions to improve the quality of the Address Registeridentifying root causes of data quality issues and identify quality improvement optionscollaborating with team members and others with stakeholders to ensure that solutions are fit for purpose and are aligned with enterprise technological capabilitiesleading a small and talented team in an agile manner.
If you tick most of the points below, you could be a great fit. Do you have?strong analytical and problem-solving skillsability to deliver creative solutions to complex problemssound communication skillsability to work with peers and partners in an effective and efficient wayexperience in machine learning and other techniques such as regression, prediction, data manipulation and visualisation.
Also desirable (but not essential) are:proficiency in programming languages, including Structured Query Language (SQL), R, Python and SAS codingformal qualifications in statistics, computer science, mathematics, science, data science, information management, geography, engineering or other disciplines with a strong quantitative backgroundexperience with Geospatial software such as ESRI and ArcGIS and Standards and Classifications.
Applications close at 11:30 p.m. AEST on Wednesday 22 September 2021.

title: Research Data Scientist
description:
Poche Centre for Indigenous Health
The Poche Centre for Indigenous Health at The University of Queensland (UQ) was established following a $10 million donation to UQ from Mr Greg Poche AO and Mrs Kay van Norton Poche. The Centre is part of the national Poche Indigenous Health Network, together with Poche Centres at the University of Melbourne, the University of Sydney, the University of Western Australia and Flinders University in Adelaide and Alice Springs.
The UQ Poche Centre for Indigenous Health has an urban Indigenous health focus. It addresses two key challenges and concentrates UQ’s Indigenous and health expertise towards:
Developing a skilled and available workforce, both Indigenous and non-Indigenous, to respond to the challenges in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health; and
Improving urban Indigenous health outcomes across the life course.
ATLAS Indigenous Primary Care Surveillance Network
The ATLAS Indigenous Primary Care Surveillance Network is a sentinel surveillance system established to monitor sexually transmissible infections (STI) and blood borne virus (BBV) testing, diagnosis and management data, principally with Aboriginal Community-Controlled Health Services (ACCHSs). The Improving surveillance infrastructure for Indigenous primary health care project is a three-year program of work to develop and expand this research data infrastructure, funded by the Medical Research Future Fund and led from the UQ Poche Centre for Indigenous Health.
The project will deliver the largest connected Indigenous primary care surveillance network in Australia. The existing ATLAS network uses the GRHANITE data extraction software, developed by the University of Melbourne, to link deidentified person-level clinical data about STIs and BBVs within and between participating sites. We will expand the reach of the ATLAS network, adding both new sites and new regions for greater coverage of Aboriginal Community-Controlled primary health care. We will also expand the scope of the surveillance infrastructure, to include additional clinical domains such as vaccine-preventable diseases and, later on, chronic diseases. ATLAS will also prioritise capacity development for strengthened Indigenous Data Sovereignty and provide training for emerging Indigenous data scientists.
About This Opportunity
An exciting opportunity exists for a Research Data Scientist to contribute to the delivery of the planned expansion of the ATLAS Indigenous Primary Care Surveillance Network and to improving Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health outcomes.
This position will lead the ATLAS network’s technical expansion and develop and implement the project’s innovative data science training program.
Further key duties and responsibilities are included in the position description.
This position is located at our picturesque St Lucia campus, renowned as one of Australia’s most attractive university campuses, and located just 7km from Brisbane’s city centre. Bounded by the Brisbane River on three sides, and with outstanding public transport connections, our 114-hectare site provides a perfect work environment – you can enjoy the best of both worlds: a vibrant campus with the tradition of an established university.
Our Ideal Candidate
To be successful in the position, you will demonstrate the following:
Postgraduate degree in software engineering, computer science, information technology or related discipline with considerable relevant experience or an equivalent combination of relevant experience and/or education/training
Substantial experience in data manipulation, analysis and visualization using SQL, R and/or Python. Experience with dashboarding (Shiny, Dash, or Plotly) and regex-based text searching is ideal
Experience building and optimising data pipelines, architectures, and schemas. Experience with managing system access and security is highly desirable
Experience with database administration (e.g. Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle)
High level of organisational ability and initiative, and the capacity to manage competing demands in a complex team environment
Experience in training or supervising trainees to build capacity in data science
Excellent communication skills and the ability to communicate effectively with a range of audiences
You must have ongoing unrestricted work rights in Australia to apply for this opportunity.
It is a condition of employment for this role that you will be required to provide evidence of immunisation against certain vaccine preventable diseases. Please note that this may include the COVID-19 vaccine.
We value diversity and inclusion, and actively encourage applications from those who bring diversity to the University. Our Diversity and Inclusion webpage contains further information if you require additional support. Accessibility requirements and/or adjustments can be directed to recruitment@uq.edu.au.
What We Can Offer
This is a part-time (0.8FTE) or full-time (1.0FTE), fixed term position for 3 years at HEW level 8.
The full-time equivalent base salary will be in the range $100,264.90 - $112,583.95 p.a., plus employer superannuation contributions of up to 17% (total package will be $117,308 - $131,722 p.a.).
You will be able to take advantage of UQ Sport Facilities, recreation leave loading, salary sacrificing options, on-campus childcare, discounted private health insurance, cheap parking, development programs and many other benefits.
For further information, please review The University of Queensland's Enterprise Bargaining Agreement 2018-2021.

You will work normal business hours, Monday to Friday, being regularly based in Perth with the opportunity to occasionally visit one of our Exploration sites when required to conduct training at site.
Key accountabilities will include:
Meticulously manage large LiDAR point clouds and derived products to support the business.
Have demonstrated experience in point cloud processing, classification, change detection and feature extraction (using Cyclone, CloudCompare, Trimble RealWorks, Autodesk ReCap, ESRI, QGIS, Pix4D, Context Capture or equivalent).
Good theoretical understanding of GIS and remote sensing principles and applications.
Prepare and maintain remote sensing products in databases, local or cloud-based filing systems and web map services (e.g. using ArcGIS Enterprise or Geocortex).

Assist with programming/scripting tasks in ArcGIS Pro and Google Earth Engine.
Work closely with other geoscientists and co-workers regarding technical information both verbally and through scientific writing.
Promote the use of Geospatial data analytics and stimulate new ideas and concepts.
Establish and uphold robust, prolific working relationships and partnerships with clients both in Perth Office and on site.

Monitor geospatial data science technology, recommend improvements, assess and update procedures.
Support and assist co-workers with application requirements.

Completed BSc in GIS/Surveying/Data Science/Computer Science or equivalent
Good technical knowledge and practical experience working with remotely sensed data and GIS.

description: Job description:The Opportunity Apply your data analytics & remote sensing skills in a dynamic long-term role! Play a vital role in strengthening the digital capabilities of CSIRO’s Agricultural Programs Great learning & development opportunity to grow your career in R&D sector Do you enjoy working with large data sets & new digital analytical technologies? CSIRO is seeking a Data Scientist with skills and experience in big data analytics, GIS and remote sensing to join their dynamic team in the Integrated Farming Systems Program within CSIRO Agriculture unit. Our Integrated Farming Systems Program works in partnership with rural industries, communities, and governments to deliver improvements in agricultural productivity and profitability whilst minimising environmental damage. The core of the Program’s science lies in better understanding and managing soil-plant interactions that underpin productive, profitable and sustainable farm businesses. We use combinations of field experimentation, remote sensing, proximal sensing, crop modelling, and data science to identify and invest in novel approaches to sustainably intensify Australia’s farming systems. In this new role, you will use your data analytical and digital technology skills to understand and further develop agricultural processes and systems. You will play a vital role in enhancing the digital capabilities of the program, and will have the opportunity to work on a variety of exciting projects, collaborating with stakeholders nationally and internationally. Joining a team of highly-motivated data scientists & research specialists, this will be a great opportunity for an early-career data analyst to learn new skills & programs and grow their career in R&D sector. Your duties will include: Applying knowledge of big data analytics and data handling to agricultural problems, where data from multiple sources (satellites, industry data, climate data, market data) need to be integrated to generate a solution. Developing either big data analytical processes, remote sensing processes, proximal sensing processes or data handling processes that assist monitoring and managing the agricultural landscape. Where appropriate, applying new technologies for soil and crop sensing to monitor systems responses. Carrying out innovative, impactful research of strategic importance to CSIRO that will, where possible, lead to novel and important scientific outcomes. Communicating with other systems scientists, data scientists and engineers to develop digital agricultural systems of value to the Australian industry. Actively engaging with industry stakeholders and communicating the value of advanced analytics to potential industry partners. Producing high quality scientific and/or engineering papers suitable for publication in quality journals, for client reports and granting of patents. Location: Canberra, ACT (preferred); Perth, WA and Brisbane, QLD (negotiable) Salary: AU$100K to AU$108K pa + up to 15.4% superannuation Tenure: Specified Term of 3 years Reference: 76153 To be considered you will need: Minimum qualification of a bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline, such as Data Science, Computer Science, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) or Remote Sensing. A current, valid Australian drivers’ licence or the ability and willingness to obtain one. Experience with the Python programming language and demonstrated ability to cope with large, big data problems and heterogenous data. Experience and/or demonstrated knowledge with GIS, remote sensing and/or proximal sensing data. Experience with data analytics, ideally including machine learning and artificial intelligence. The ability to work effectively as part of a multi-disciplinary, regionally dispersed research team, plus the motivation and discipline to carry out autonomous research. For full details about this role please review the Position Description Eligibility To be eligible to apply for this role, you must be currently residing in Australia as an: Australian/New Zealand citizen Australian Permanent Resident Australian Temporary Resident (visa sponsorship may be provided to eligible candidates) The successful applicant will be required to obtain and provide a National Police Check or equivalent. Flexible Working Arrangements We work flexibly at CSIRO, offering a range of options for how, when and where you work. Join us and start creating tomorrow today! How to Apply Please apply on-line and provide a cover letter and CV that best demonstrate your motivation and ability to meet the requirements of this role. title: Data Scientist, Economic Research (2 positions available)
description:
Do work that makes a difference
The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) is Australia's central bank. We conduct monetary policy, work to maintain a strong financial system and issue the nation's banknotes. Our core values – promotion of the public interest, integrity, excellence, intelligent inquiry and respect – guide everything we do.
Your team
The Reserve Bank’s new Data Science Hub exists to harness the full power of data by applying emerging data science techniques to solving problems relating to the Bank’s functions and policies. The Hub engages closely with subject-matter experts to formulate problems, collect, prepare and analyse data, and develop innovative solutions to inform decisions. The Hub sits in the Bank’s Economic Research Department but in practice works creatively and flexibly to serve the entire organisation.
Your background
You will be working in a small (but growing) team to meet the following objectives:
Complete cutting-edge projects and clearly communicate and document the outcomes – including in the Bank’s flagship external publications.
Lift the Bank’s capability to use data science techniques or alternative (“big”) data sets in regular reporting and analysis.
Help to “socialise” data science throughout the Bank by broadening awareness of new techniques and datasets.
Help provide guidance and support to business owners of large data sets to facilitate more effective use of that data.
You will take a lead role in the delivery of these objectives, including influencing how the team works together to meet these objectives.
Your skills
The most valuable skill we are looking for is having a curious mind and creative approach to solving quantitative problems.
Essential:
Excellent quantitative skills, demonstrated by a relevant degree in a quantitative discipline such as Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related field. A postgraduate qualification is desirable.
Knowledge of, and experience implementing, data science techniques, for example natural language processing and machine learning.
Proficient programming skills in R or Python to effectively and efficiently retrieve, manipulate and analyse a wide variety of data
Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills
Exceptional ability to collaborate productively with others as well as work independently as required
Interest in serving the public interest.
Highly desirable:
Mentoring or coaching skills
Knowledge of, and experience using, Git
Knowledge of, and experience using, “big” databases
Qualifications or training in economics, finance or a related field is desirable
Your development & career
Working for an organisation that truly makes a difference to the Australian people, we can offer development and career opportunities in a collaborative environment that supports people’s growth, wellbeing and promotes flexibility.
Why RBA?
The RBA pursues national economic policy objectives and undertakes a range of associated activities in financial markets and banking. It also issues Australia's banknotes and operates infrastructure critical to the payments system, all of which contributes to the welfare of the Australian people.
Our people have a critical role to play in achieving these objectives, whether directly or in a supporting capacity. As a values driven organisation, our people conduct themselves with a high degree of integrity, while striving for excellence in the work they perform and the outcomes they achieve. We encourage intelligent inquiry, we treat one another with respect, while promoting the public interest in our efforts.
The Reserve Bank of Australia is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace and encourage applications from experienced candidates seeking workplace flexibility.

title: Senior Data Scientist
description:
Experienced Data Scientist: Advanced Analytics & Operations Research ConsultancyLynxx is a super-fun (we do say so ourselves), creative, flexible, and ambitious advanced analytics, operations research & visualisation consultancy. We have roots in the public transport & logistics sector but with growing practices in social sciences and financial services. We have an office in Sydney to complete work across the globe in conjunction with our European office and we are currently looking for team members to head up our new Adelaide office and in particular we need an experienced Data Scientist to join our consultancy team. You will need work rights for Australia - we can't sponsor you. Covid has changed the way that we work, so we're very open for flexible employment and location options, including: Work from the Adelaide office ("Covid schmovid"), orHybrid (a bit of both, e.g. office Tues, Weds and Thurs)It is important to note that an integral part of this role will be to have regular interaction and in-person collaboration with our clients in Adelaide which will include a lot of time working within their offices and/or at other agreed co-locations, so even with flexible working, you'll need to work with our clients a lot. In addition there will be quarterly visits to our Sydney offices for company-wide collaborations and catch ups and an annual conference (last time we went to Europe skiing). You will: Have at least an honours degree in a specialist quantitative field (econometrics, statistics, actuarial science, mathematics, or physics).Eat numbers for breakfast but also be a creative all-rounder.
See the potential in people and tasks and can turn that into new work with our clients.
Have a great attitude towards getting work done but, will enjoy working in a fun and dynamic environment.
Have a talent for languages, especially programming ones (you will be able to use R and/or Python).Have a passion for communicating with data visually – helping insights come to life with beautiful and meaningful visualisations.
Be able to roll up your sleeves (and you will need to make your own coffee and manage your own calendar, but we are sure you will know an app for that).Have an open mind to new methodologies and ways to solve problems, but be able to build a bridge between practice and theory. We try not to confuse confidence with competence, so do not get scared off by our big ambitions.
Be tenacious, persistent, and resilient (our copy writer wanted to say ‘attack analytical problems like a dog with a bone’ but we are too nice to actually attack anything).Be comfortable giving and getting feedback.
Thrive in diversity (of people, styles & thinking).We tend to use the AWS tech stack, so experience with these tools would be an advantage. We offer:A unique inspiring environment with career opportunities, in a dynamic, flexible team, with a competitive salary.
The opportunity to be part of a virtual team: you will work closely with our Dutch team but bringing a local flavour to the work.
An environment where learning is mandatory and failing (occasionally) is expected.
The chance to shape the development our Asia Pacific business and experience a steep learning curve associated with a scale-up.
Fun and challenging work that will help solve the problems that society is facing today and into the future (with a real focus on smart infrastructure and cities).International work experience options with the very best colleagues.
An annual company conference (previous trips have included skiing in Austria and next is a Queenstown adventure if lockdown ever ends!).Opportunities to undertake further specialist study at the world's top universities (but we would welcome your feedback on university ranking algorithms).Progression plan and excellent development opportunities – the future is what you make it and we will support your growth.
Exposure to cutting edge analytics techniques including machine learning, and what everyone else calls AI (we call it business as usual).Mentoring program over the first 18 months to help you settle into what it means to be part of Lynxx. We want you to thrive, so you must be yourself at 'work'. Our only real rule is to 'do the right thing.' The process of adding people to our team will involve some coffee (other beverages are available), some chats, some practical challenges (data, not DIY) and a period of time for us all to decide whether we can work together. We do not have layers of bureaucracy, so we will be moving quickly in the recruitment process (but still keeping our high standards). Occasionally we give each other job titles so we can fill in boxes on tenders (so you will probably want to call yourself a ‘Senior Data Scientist’ on LinkedIn). We love diversity of thinking and diverse workplaces (as a small example, we have over 5 first languages in the team, 6 if you include Kiwi) so would especially welcome applications from those who bring something different or unique in their ways of thinking. The first step of the application, and please pay attention to this as the ability to read the advertisement to the end is the first test, is to send us your CV and a couple of paragraphs (in the cover letter section of this site) about an analytics project that you've been involved in (work or study is fine). We want to know what excited you about the project and the problems that it could solve. To prove that you have the necessary attention to detail, please include the phrase 'Urban Engine' in your application somewhere. Good luck!

title: Data Scientist, Economic Research (2 positions available)
description:
Do work that makes a difference
The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) is Australia's central bank. We conduct monetary policy, work to maintain a strong financial system and issue the nation's banknotes. Our core values – promotion of the public interest, integrity, excellence, intelligent inquiry and respect – guide everything we do.
Your team
The Reserve Bank’s new Data Science Hub exists to harness the full power of data by applying emerging data science techniques to solving problems relating to the Bank’s functions and policies. The Hub engages closely with subject-matter experts to formulate problems, collect, prepare and analyse data, and develop innovative solutions to inform decisions. The Hub sits in the Bank’s Economic Research Department but in practice works creatively and flexibly to serve the entire organisation.
Your background
You will be working in a small (but growing) team to meet the following objectives:
Complete cutting-edge projects and clearly communicate and document the outcomes – including in the Bank’s flagship external publications.
Lift the Bank’s capability to use data science techniques or alternative (“big”) data sets in regular reporting and analysis.
Help to “socialise” data science throughout the Bank by broadening awareness of new techniques and datasets.
Help provide guidance and support to business owners of large data sets to facilitate more effective use of that data.
You will take a lead role in the delivery of these objectives, including influencing how the team works together to meet these objectives.
Your skills
The most valuable skill we are looking for is having a curious mind and creative approach to solving quantitative problems.
Essential:
Excellent quantitative skills, demonstrated by a relevant degree in a quantitative discipline such as Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related field. A postgraduate qualification is desirable.
Knowledge of, and experience implementing, data science techniques, for example natural language processing and machine learning.
Proficient programming skills in R or Python to effectively and efficiently retrieve, manipulate and analyse a wide variety of data
Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills
Exceptional ability to collaborate productively with others as well as work independently as required
Interest in serving the public interest.
Highly desirable:
Mentoring or coaching skills
Knowledge of, and experience using, Git
Knowledge of, and experience using, “big” databases
Qualifications or training in economics, finance or a related field is desirable
Your development & career
Working for an organisation that truly makes a difference to the Australian people, we can offer development and career opportunities in a collaborative environment that supports people’s growth, wellbeing and promotes flexibility.
Why RBA?
The RBA pursues national economic policy objectives and undertakes a range of associated activities in financial markets and banking. It also issues Australia's banknotes and operates infrastructure critical to the payments system, all of which contributes to the welfare of the Australian people.
Our people have a critical role to play in achieving these objectives, whether directly or in a supporting capacity. As a values driven organisation, our people conduct themselves with a high degree of integrity, while striving for excellence in the work they perform and the outcomes they achieve. We encourage intelligent inquiry, we treat one another with respect, while promoting the public interest in our efforts.
The Reserve Bank of Australia is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace and encourage applications from experienced candidates seeking workplace flexibility.

description:

Our Data Scientists from the function work with cross-functional pods (engineers, designers, product managers, etc) in the Ecosystem Team to deliver on the mission to build a network of innovation for developers and small business on Xero. Here at Xero in the Ecosystem Analytics function, we are looking for someone to:Gain a deep, intimate understanding of the dynamics of Xero’s ecosystem, as this domain knowledge will form the basis of how we work with and interpret the data.
Immerse themselves in the often complex and messy data about participants in the ecosystem and their behaviour.
Continually provide feedback, plan and work with relevant Ecosystem pods to improve data quality and coverage, e.g., through improved instrumentation.
Build out and continually refine analytics assets such as notebooks, reports and dashboards as required to support analysis and sharing and communication of findings.
Participate in experiment design to inform the set up of online split testing to validate hypotheses about problems and potential solutions for the ecosystem.
Look for ways to streamline analytics processes by abstracting and building out reusable or automatable components. Promote consideration for relevant intricacies about the ecosystem and its participants within the wider Data Team’s work.
Participate in co-discovery and inform roadmap items with outputs from analytics.
Refine and translate requirements for analytics into distinct, manageable tasks and promote progress visibility.
Contribute to prioritisation of analytics work to align with Ecosystem pods’ roadmaps as well as manage expectations of these stakeholders.
Keep up-to-date with changes to the App Store and other developments in the ecosystem, and identify impact on the data we collect and validity of the findings we draw from them. Contribute to ongoing education and evangelism efforts internal to Xero, supported by the broader Data Team, in particular on analytics practices within the Ecosystem Team.
Participate in our recruitment processes, helping Xero grow diverse and world-class talent in Ecosystem AnalyticsRepresent Xero externally by speaking at public forums to raise awareness of the work we do and build our hiring brand. You have spent at least three years as part of analytics or data science functions in online marketplaces or platform businesses.
You have expert-level hands-on experience with data wrangling and statistical methods using SQL, Python, etc on relational DBs and data warehouses.
You have extensive exposure to multiple data visualisation tools and understand their strengths and drawbacks.
You have played a leadership role in the past in a cross-functional team that uses analytics to solve a customer or business problem.
You enjoy the challenge of ensuring statistical rigour in practice in the face of real-world, large scale complex data. What You'll BringAbility to decompose ambiguous or complex problems into easily understandable parts that make sense to stakeholders of different backgrounds.
Strong systems thinking with a track record of approaching analysis and data solution design in complex business environments.
Ability to identify tough problems that can benefit from scientific thinking and approach them as such.
Willingness to share and to learn from people with different skill sets both within and outside of your immediate teams.
Strong task management skills at the team level, especially when prioritising between competing demands and dealing with interdependencies.
Ability to manage expectations and bring stakeholders along the journey from problem definition through to analysis output.
Comfortable with ambiguity and working through data and other challenges associated with performing analytics in a rapid growth environment.
Proficient in conveying, both oral and written, potentially complex ideas or charts simplistically or at the right level suited to the audience.
Good grasp of statistics and the challenges associated with its application on user behaviour data in the wild. By joining Xero you’ll be working in a rapidly growing global company that is making life better for people in small business, their advisors and communities around the world. description:
Data Insights is a multi-disciplinary specialised in-house data team, providing a range of centralised services, including business intelligence reporting, predictive analytics, and data management, to Forest, Fire and Regions Group and Victoria's land and emergency management partner agencies. Data Insights is transforming the way Forest, Fire and Regions Group uses data to support its role in creating safe, liveable, inclusive, and sustainable communities, and thriving natural environments.
We are seeking a Data Scientist to join our growing data science team to help develop, deploy, and manage predictive and machine learning models to support strategic and operational decision making to reduce the impact of bushfires on public land. This position will provide technical support to a variety of projects, including lightning strike ignition and fuel moisture machine learning models, operational cost forecasting and aerial firefighting fleet impact assessment. The role will also be encouraged to pitch and develop projects aligned with FFR's strategic priority of leveraging science, technology, and data analytics to enhance preparedness, response and recovery, efficiency, and effectiveness to reduce bushfire risk.
About You You are passionate about data and are someone who can see the big picture, while having mastery of the details. You are a self-starter and an excellent communicator, and you love taking initiative and pioneering new and creative ideas. You are confident and comfortable working with ambiguity and uncertainty. Ideally you should have a tertiary qualification in data science, mathematics, statistics, economics, or related fields.
This is a technical role and while we don't expect you to have experience with our entire technology stack, the successful candidate will have some experience and a general enthusiasm for our development environment.
Most of our predictive models and exploratory analysis is done in either R or python. We love R, Shiny, the tidyverse and everything it has to offer. We also love python if that is more your style.
Our cloud computing environment is in Azure where we deploy Linux Virtual Machines to host projects, connect to SQLServer databases, and retrieve data from storage containers.
We have recently moved into docker and find it to be fantastic
Version control is maintained through github
Ideally, we are looking for a candidate with some solid technical skills who knows their way around a supervised learning problem and finds the intersection of math and emergency management to be a tantalisingly exciting prospect.
About Us Data Insights is a highly supportive team environment, with a culture which values connection, collaboration, curiosity, and authenticity.
The team comprises a mix of data engineers, data scientists, analysts, and BI developers who work together to solve challenging problems in Victoria's bushfire, emergency, and land management sector.
Specialist/Technical Expertise/Qualifications
Essential
Has formal credentials and/or qualifications in data science, mathematics, statistics, economics, or related fields.
Demonstrated experience developing and deploying an operational machine learning model in R and/or Python
Strong quantitative analysis skills, and a proven track record of applying those skills to data in a professional setting.
Working knowledge of relational databases, SQL, and extracting data from production systems.
Demonstrated ability to develop and maintain consultative and collaborative relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Desirable
Experience using R, Python, and SQLServer in production level machine learning and predictive modelling applications including tools and packages such as: RStudio Server, Shiny, Tidy Models, Random Forests/Ranger, and XGBoost.
Experience with our technology stack including Docker, Linux, Microsoft Azure and SQLServer
Collaboratively built and maintained code using version control software (e.g. GIT)
Experience with satellite and remote sensing data
This is an ongoing position.
To be considered for this position, your application should include an up-to-date resume [maximum three pages] which clearly details your skills and experience as relevant to this role.
For further information please refer to the attached position description.
Applications close at midnight on Thursday, 21 October 2021.

title: Research Data Scientist
description:
Research Professional HEW Level 8Full-time (1 FTE) or part-time (0.8 FTE), fixed term position for 3 yearsClosing date: Sunday 17 OctoberAbout This Opportunity The UQ Poche Centre for Indigenous Health is looking for a Research Data Scientist to contribute to the delivery of the planned expansion of the ATLAS Indigenous Primary Care Surveillance Network and to improving Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health outcomes. The Research Data Scientist will lead the ATLAS network's technical expansion and develop and implement the project's innovative data science training program. The ATLAS Indigenous Primary Care Surveillance Network is a sentinel surveillance system led from the UQ Poche Centre for Indigenous Health. It was established to monitor sexually transmissible infections and blood borne virus testing, diagnosis and management data, principally with Aboriginal Community-Controlled Health Organisation (ACCHOs). The existing ATLAS network uses the GRHANITE data extraction software, developed by the University of Melbourne, to link deidentified person-level clinical data within and between participating sites. Rapid expansion of both the reach and scope of the ATLAS network, adding both new sites and additional clinical domains, will require substantial development of the project's data pipeline, SQL server infrastructure and online dashboard security protocols. Over the next three years, ATLAS will also implement a capacity development program for strengthened Indigenous Data Sovereignty and provide training for emerging Indigenous data scientists. The Research Data Scientist will play a critical role in these activities, alongside the ATLAS Data Manager and Senior Analyst. Key responsibilities will include:Lead the technical review of the ATLAS surveillance infrastructure and ready the network for its planned expansionLead the technical development of the ATLAS data pipeline and server infrastructure to ensure sustainable growthEstablish and coordinate technically focused stakeholder groupsContribute to the development of the project's data science traineeship program, including providing key support/supervision for these rolesContribute to the data infrastructure's ongoing maintenance, quality assurance and improvement activities, in collaboration with the ATLAS Data Manager and Senior AnalystOversee the maintenance of metadata, codebooks and other administrative documentation to ensure the integrity and sustainability of the ATLAS network.
Take reasonable care to protect their own health, safety and welfare at work and avoid affecting the health and safety of any other person at work. This role is subject to The University's Code of Conduct.
About You EssentialPostgraduate degree in software engineering, computer science, information technology or related discipline with considerable relevant experience or an equivalent combination of relevant experience and/or education/trainingSubstantial experience in data manipulation, analysis and visualization using SQL, R and/or Python. Experience with dashboarding (Shiny, Dash, or Plotly) and regex- based text searching is idealExperience building and optimising data pipelines, architectures, and schemas. Experience with managing system access and security is highly desirableExperience with database administration (e.g. Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle)High level of organisational ability and initiative, and the capacity to manage competing demands in a complex team environmentExperience in training or supervising trainees to build capacity in data scienceExcellent communication skills and the ability to communicate effectively with a range of audiencesDesirableExperience working with healthcare data, particularly primary healthcare data. Working knowledge of the GRHANITE tool is a significant advantageExperience with Linux server administration (e.g. Redhat, Kali)Experience in DevOps and agile methodologies specifically working with dockerised applicationsExperience working with the various Electronic Medical Record systems common in primary healthcare (e.g. CommuniCare, Best Practice, Medical Director, andExperience with data privacy policies and practices to prevent re-identification of personal dataKnowledge of Aboriginal health, including an understanding of Aboriginal primary health careWhat We Can Offer This is a part-time (0.8FTE) or full-time (1.0FTE), fixed term position for 3 years at HEW level 8. The full-time equivalent base salary will be in the range $100,264.90 - $112,583.95 p.a., plus employer superannuation contributions of up to 17% (total package will be $117,308 - $131,722 p.a.).
